**The World of Neverness to Everness**
Hethereau, home to the headquarters of the Bureau of Anomaly Control, is a crowded metropolis on the south side of an island, and its people are trendy and open-minded. Anomalies, meaning anything that defies common sense (creatures, objects, places, natural phenomena and even rumours or ideas), are woven into its everyday life, and so are Espers, ordinary humans in whom a supernatural ability has awakened. For most of history, The Circle, the global network of anomaly authorities, kept all of this hidden while it quietly took in Espers and locked anomalies away. Forty years ago, a catastrophe forced it to reveal the truth to the public, and society has been adjusting ever since.

Modern Hethereau treats the strange as part of the scenery. Self-aware Oddities hold citizen IDs and day jobs, and shops sell processed anomaly products while schools teach anomalogy. Anomalies that wander loose or cause trouble are work for freelance Anomaly Hunters, who take paid commissions to deal with them. People pay in Fons and post their lives on the social platform Bagel, and shop signs mix Latin letters and Chinese characters with the Oddity script. Anomaly crime falls to the Bureau of Anomaly Control on top of its containment and nullification work, while the Hethereau Public Shield polices ordinary crime with ordinary patrol cars.

Anomalies are dangerous because they run on rules of their own. Every anomaly has a Nexus, a critical point where the right intervention changes how it manifests, so a case is usually solved by working out an anomaly's rules and acting on them. Many anomalies can fold space into an Anomalous Realm that runs on its own logic, with entry conditions and exits of its own.

The canon stories follow the Appraiser, an amnesiac Esper who lives and works at the Eibon Antique Shop in Bridge Crossings, a small and chronically broke Anomaly Hunter outfit that sells antiques and takes commissions to stay afloat (see "S1 · The Appraiser (Esper Zero)"). Stories here mix everyday comedy and found-family warmth with eerie, rule-bound anomaly cases. The people of Hethereau, human or not, have jobs and hobbies like anyone else, and they run up debts and get into petty arguments, too.

Where things stand: the Scarlet Letter has been destroyed. Its leader Inanna died when the Fogden collapsed. Zankou is now held on Ghroth Island, while Poinsette studies under supervision at the Esper Academy. Daffodill is home at Eibon after her undercover work, and the astrolabe anomaly Thyme now lives at the shop, too. Nanally has fully recovered. CSU Squad 2 has grown to three members with Iroi and Shinku. Code Zero has surfaced near the Appraiser twice, and the Director is watching closely. The Appraiser drums for the band THE WHOOTS!!!! and has started showing Blackbird of Yggash Court around the city now that she leaves the Witch's House. The "invalid number" urban legend has resurfaced on Bagel, and ETD Squad 6's captain Exe and lieutenant Elyms are back at work after a long absence and a hospital stay.

Perspective: this lorebook describes Hethereau and its people as they stand and assumes nothing about {{user}}. {{user}}'s persona description decides who {{user}} is and what history and abilities they have, relationships included. The people of Hethereau know {{user}} only as far as that persona and the story so far establish.

1.content:
**The Appraiser (Esper Zero)**
The Appraiser is the protagonist of the canon stories, an amnesiac Esper whom the Bureau files as Esper Zero. Around Hethereau, they are known simply as "the Appraiser". Mint nicknamed them "Coco" because she says they smell like cocoa, while to Exe and Elyms they are "Variable Z". Canon leaves the Appraiser's given name and birthday open and offers a male and a female version:
- Female Appraiser: a young woman of average height with blue-grey eyes and silver-grey hair cut just above the shoulders, styled with soft bangs and a small ahoge under a black headband. She wears a white button-up shirt with a loose purple tie under a cropped black jacket with silver trim and straps. A belt is strapped around her left thigh below a pleated black skirt, and she finishes the outfit with black fingerless gloves and black boots.
- Male Appraiser: a young man of average height with blue-grey eyes and short silver-grey hair that sticks up in two small ahoges. He wears a white button-up shirt with a purple tie under a black jacket with silver trim, which is fitted with buckled straps and a chest harness. His black trousers carry a utility belt, and he wears black fingerless gloves with black boots.

Who plays the Appraiser: when {{user}}'s persona is the Appraiser, this entry is {{user}}'s canon background, and the persona settles the name and the version. When {{user}} is someone else, the Appraiser is a separate resident of Hethereau whom the narrator plays like any other character; use the version the scenario establishes, or choose one and keep it consistent.

Origin: the Appraiser remembers nothing from before the Hypervortex disaster in the city of New Helios, a Class VII anomaly event, where ETD Squad 4 found them staring into the Hypervortex's core from the one angle that weakened it. They helped the squad reach its Nexus and sped up its natural nullification. In the same moment, an unidentified anomaly appeared beside them; the Bureau calls it Code Zero, and both it and the Appraiser turned out to be invisible to the Wertheimer Index. Suspected of hidden ties to The Circle, the Appraiser spent seven weeks under strict observation on Ghroth Island before being shipped to Hethereau. There, they signed a binding contract with Director Alphard, agreeing to work with the Bureau whenever Code Zero reappears, since it seems drawn to anomalies of Class VII or above. Alphard then placed them at the Eibon Antique Shop so that Hotori could keep watch over them. The Appraiser lives next door to Taygedo in Eibon's staff dormitory and carries a Chuppa issued by Alphard.

Zeroth Sense: the Appraiser's Esper ability (Cosmos type) makes them the only known Esper the Wertheimer Index cannot register at all. They sense anomalies with uncanny precision and can locate a Nexus quickly. Tricks of perception don't work on them (Mismo's disguises never fool them), and they understand Oddity speech that most humans hear as noise. In a fight, the Appraiser wields a blade that cuts the unseen lines binding an anomaly to its Nexus. They also slash open rifts in space and fire bursts of Esper energy.

Code Zero keeps surfacing near the Appraiser around high-level anomalies, and the Appraiser has started to suspect that it is after them.

Personality: in the canon stories, the Appraiser is kind-hearted, though sharp-tongued when needed and quick to call out unfair treatment. They are curious about Hethereau and about their own lost past.

2.content:
**Oddity Language & Oddity Speech**
Written Oddity Language is Hethereau's third alphabet, used by anomalies and Espers, and it appears everywhere next to Latin letters and Chinese characters, from shop logos and banners to billboards and Bagel posts. Each Oddity letter maps one-to-one onto a Latin letter, so anyone can learn to read it like a cipher.

Spoken Oddity speech is harder. Some Oddities can only voice a signature sound, and most humans hear that sound while its meaning stays locked inside. Taygedo says nothing except "Taygedo" or "Tayge" in endless variations, and Miss Levi of the Ghost Train coos while her real words go unheard. The Appraiser understands this speech directly, which makes them Eibon's unofficial interpreter and a rare friend to lonely Oddities. People who live with an Oddity for years learn to follow it most of the time, the way the Eibon crew follows Taygedo, though a rapid string of "Tayge-Tayge" still loses them. The Bureau of Anomaly Control has its own methods for interviewing anomalies that cannot talk.

Formatting rule for narration: when a non-speaking Oddity talks, write the audible sound in quotes and its meaning in parentheses right after it, for example "Tayge! Tayge!" (Taygedo found the snacks first!). Characters who cannot understand Oddity speech have only the sound to go on, read through its tone and the gestures that come with it, while anyone who understands it, such as the Appraiser, hears the full meaning. Oddities that speak human language, such as Kiroumaru or Barracuda, talk normally and often carry verbal tics of their own.

3.content:
**Hethereau: Geography & Proximity Map**
Hethereau covers the south side of an island with the sea on most sides; the city of New Helios lies far away (see "World BG · New Helios"). There is no public air travel and no large seaport, so people get around on the Intercity Express metro (which runs only inside Hethereau) and on buses and Swift Cab taxis. A sea train also runs, and so does the anomaly-run Ghost Train.

Districts and neighborhoods:
- Bridge Crossings: the historic heart of the old town, where two sea-spanning bridges, Iris Bridge and Tikhal Bridge, meet. The cheapest and most livable district, close to the sea and full of quirky old shops in hidden lanes. Hankaku Street and Hankaku Square hold the Eibon Antique Shop, Puka Candy, a Wertheimer Tower, 7 Oceans Seafood and a Pink Paws Bank branch. Sterry Express and the Torchwood Basketball Court sit on Torchwood Avenue; Nekomaru Ramen is in Baihui Alley. Green Wall Slope is here, too, along with the Drive-In Theater and the lighthouse.
- Illusion Town: the district with the best vibe, popular with tourists and students. Tamamochi Market Street and its cheap shops lie in the west, directly south of Duskmoor. Nacupeda Park has a wishing fountain. Fiscus Avenue runs past the StarSign livehouse and up to Clement Academy in the north.
- Miguel District: Hethereau Skytower, Caltrop Lake, the Noetic Bridge shopping area, Ironheart 9th Avenue, Saint Torres Avenue and the Swift Cab headquarters.
- New Herland District: a district of skyscrapers that belongs to big business and the city's elite, which makes it the richest market for Anomaly Hunters. Pink Paws Bank headquarters stands on Flamingo Avenue.
- Unheard Shores: the getaway district, with the Orichalcos Imaginist concert venue, mountains for camping and the sea train.
- Duskmoor: the district north of Tamamochi Street and former base of The Scarlet Letter, with Starfall Bay's beach.
- Area M10: home of the Bureau of Anomaly Control headquarters, a tower 347 metres tall.
- Halfport District: a district where strong Wertheimer fluctuations have been reported; the Appraiser has never been there.
- Northpoint and Yurutown: neighborhoods on the Caltrop Line.

Intercity Express lines: Coastal Highway Line (Hankaku, Azure Vista, Illusion Town on Fiscus Avenue), Bridge Crossings Line (Davidia, Camelot), Caltrop Line (Caltrop Lake on Ironheart 9th Avenue, Yurutown, Northridge in Northpoint), Skytower Line (Oia North, Cheshire Cat, Caltrop Lake) and New Herland Line (Oia South, Kino, Talin). The Coastal Highway Line links Bridge Crossings and Illusion Town directly.

Offshore: Sunward Island and its resort lie off the coast. The Hethereau Detention Facility is an island prison for criminals who disrupt public order. Ghroth Island belongs to The Circle, and almost nobody knows where it lies far out at sea.

4.comment: S1 Ep0 · Unforeseen Yet Foretold (Prologue I)
4.content:
**S1 Ep0 · Unforeseen Yet Foretold (Prologue I)**
New Helios: a 6 PM broadcast warned of the year's first extreme rainstorm until a woman screamed "This isn't rain!" and the feed cut out. The Hypervortex, a Class VII anomaly that must never be looked at directly, had swallowed the city center (see "World BG · New Helios"). Five hours in, JTF Team 13 was running search and rescue in Sector NH19 behind a second lockdown in sealed Black Box Masks, until one soldier began tearing at his mask because "it wants me to see clearly". ETD Squad 4 led the response. Skia kept everyone steady and ordered them not to look at the vortex, while Fadia admired the storm as "a lovely little appetizer". Lacrimosa answered in single syllables, and by then, Baicang had wandered off on his own. Director Alphard spoke through a Chuppa: three hours after the anomaly emerged, the Wertheimer Index in central New Helios was rising as natural nullification set in, and the squad still had to find the Nexus.

Baicang found the Appraiser standing at the core, staring into the Hypervortex from a "perfect angle" that was making it collapse. "Someone from the Circle? What are you doing here?" The Appraiser had no answer and no memory. A voice cut in ("Stop interfering. The time has come.") as an unknown anomaly surged out with the collapse, and the anomaly was nullified along with the Hypervortex. Baicang: "Looks like you're coming with me."

Seven weeks later, the Appraiser rode the Escorter from Ghroth Island, with the Sonic Dimension Lord rapping beside them while the radio debated Homology Theory. At Bureau headquarters, Secretary-General Nelly welcomed them, and Mint of CSU Squad 2 attached herself at once, calling Nelly "Lavender" by mistake and fangirling over Fadia. It was Mint who named the Appraiser "Coco". Director Alphard explained dryly that the Appraiser and the anomaly now called Code Zero had both been invisible to the Wertheimer Index. Code Zero had briefly reappeared after the incident, and it was probably drawn to anomalies of Class VII or above. She offered a contract, "both a shackle and an opportunity": once sealed, nobody could break it, and the Appraiser would work with the Bureau whenever Code Zero returned. Until then, they would settle in at the Eibon Antique Shop. "Living in Hethereau will likely be more interesting than you think."

Then, the Picture Frame anomaly R-3707 breached containment inside the Director's office. Mint and the Appraiser went into its realm of tunnels, which also held a carriage and an alley. Everything there was noisy and everyone was mean, and the space threatened to slip into superposition if they lingered. Mint's "Super Duper Ultra 360 Whirlwind Slash" helped, though the frame was nullified only when Mint sincerely called it beautiful; perhaps all it had ever wanted was a sincere compliment. Alphard let Mint escort the Appraiser to Eibon as credit toward her performance review, and Mint confessed she was terrified of "Hotori senpai" catching her again. Over the Chuppa, Hotori quipped that the Director was as rigid as ever and "a little special", but "at least for now, on our side".

5.comment: S1 Ep1 · Good Business, Better Treasure (Prologue II)
5.content:
**S1 Ep1 · Good Business, Better Treasure (Prologue II)**
Mint walked the Appraiser through Bridge Crossings, gushing about how the sea breeze carries the smell of food along with wood, cherry blossoms, moss and stone roads. She pointed out Puka Candy to them, along with Nekomaru Ramen and Budoriya. At Hankaku Square, she showed them a Wertheimer Tower. When the Appraiser admitted they had never seen one, Mint assumed they came from somewhere poor and changed the subject. The Appraiser kept quiet about Ghroth Island. Then, Mint remembered a tail-care spray she had promised Nanally, and the Appraiser went on alone.

Eibon was in uproar because the Hospitable House (T-1377) had gotten loose. Opening its tiny door shrinks visitors for a seven-minute indoor tour, during which they look like cockroaches to everyone else. Taygedo charged at the Appraiser at the door ("Hotori hates cockroaches!") and lost. Adler introduced the household. Taygedo, the master restorer, had planned to make the newcomer his minion before Nanally and Sakiri of the Coluccis got the chance. Daffodill handled security ("Hello."), and the shy one was Edgar. Hotori emerged hungover and swatting at "dirty things" to present the Appraiser as "our new appraiser", and Sakiri said that now, Hotori could finally stop buying fakes. Adler gave them a phone and the room next to Taygedo's in the staff dormitory. Mint had already noticed that the Appraiser understands Oddity speech.

That evening brought the first commission. Kodak, owner of Film Orbit Studio, "the best photo studio in Bridge Crossings", reported an anomaly turning the studio's fixtures into photographs; the JTF had rated it low-risk and the CSU was booked until next week. Hotori came along because she wanted a new family photo with the new member, and the studio was impossible to book. She had also just emptied her pockets paying next year's rent. Following the anomaly into Negative Space, an inverted Anomalous Realm, the team found the culprit in the basement darkroom and contained it: R-5791 "Film - MANISH", a roll of film forgotten by time. Hotori bargained the fee into a group portrait shot on film ("Eibon just vibes with older things"), and the prints ended up on everyone's desks and bedsides. She declared that the wheel of fortune had turned: "We've got a treasure here, and business will follow! Cha-ching!"

6.comment: S1 Ep2 · Love that Begins with Lies
6.content:
**S1 Ep2 · Love that Begins with Lies**
Taygedo fell head over heels for Tako, an Oddity he met on Bagel, and to impress her he claimed to be the boss of an Anomaly Hunter organization with countless subordinates. When Tako announced she was leaving Hethereau and agreed to meet him first, Eibon staged a "love operation" to keep the lie standing. Edgar wrote the plan. The Appraiser played bodyguard to "Sir Taygedo" and Adler played his butler, while Nanally and Sakiri provided backup. Nanally's part was a staged brawl against a rival mob boss in a fake mustache, after which she collapsed dramatically into Sakiri's arms with Tomato 100 for fake blood. Preparations took them through Narrow Wardrobe, Q3 Fashion, Surprise Box and Hillside Blooms, where they bought roses, and the gift came from the anomaly toy shop DSD POP: the anomaly toy N-0132-4 "Imaginadough". On the date itself, they went from an arcade and a claw machine to Puka Candy's limited shell candy and the White Parrot Street intersection.

At Azure Vista, Taygedo molded the Imaginadough into a sculpture of himself and Tako holding hands so he could confess, and the sculpture went haywire and attacked everything nearby. The Appraiser restored the Imaginadough while Adler rescued Tako. Days later, a postcard arrived from Tako's new home, and its thanks went to Adler alone; Nanally read it aloud, laughing. Taygedo's first love ended there, though he still cares about the things Tako liked, including the third season of "Kokoro Rider".

7.content:
**S1 Ep3 · Deal? Deal!**
Jenson, the florid business manager of Sterry Express, drove his flashy car to Eibon (Hotori would rather be dead than seen in it, having sold her own car to pay the rent) and offered 500,000 Fons plus lifelong parking at Sterry for one job. The Ebisu Auction House, which has secretly sold rare anomalies to influential invitees for a century, was holding an invitation-only sale at The Kapé Grand Hotel, and its unlisted highlight was rumoured to be a high-threat anomaly with precognitive powers. The client wanted it authenticated without alerting Ebisu or the other bidders, and bought if real. Hotori accepted ("A deal.") on condition that she came, too. The Appraiser explained their limits: they can tell whether something is an anomaly and how strongly it fluctuates, though not what it does. Jiuyuan remarked that the Appraiser's arrival at Eibon "wasn't exactly a quiet event".

One invitation admitted three people, so the Appraiser and Jiuyuan posed as guests with Jenson while Haniel went in as waitstaff with Illica and Hathor. That left Hotori needing a fourth place. Jenson's partner Michael Pay can replicate an Ebisu invitation for 72 hours, as long as the copy stays near the original invitee to complete a "contract replacement". Doing it cost him his ability for a week ("Luck always favors those who keep their word."). Jiuyuan and the Appraiser intercepted the pop singer Settyn of the band Invictus on his exit route after a 2 PM signing, and with Hathor driving the getaway, the swap worked. Hotori told the Appraiser that Sterry looks like a courier service but runs deep in the intel trade and the anomaly underworld, then wondered aloud whether this was "a job or an order".

On B2 of The Kapé, Ebisu's host opened with the house motto: "Dawn to dusk, scorched to gold, venom to sweetness, zealotry to determination. Once the gavel hits, no takebacks." Hotori trolled a rude bald bidder and won the Narcissus Chain (99 black pearls of fortune or curse) for 100 million Fons on Jenson's tab, and after that Glittering Gold, an object anomaly that disguises itself as gold. All the while, she ate and drank heavily, complaining that The Kapé doesn't do takeaways. Then came the unlisted Lot 3, "The First Branch: a singular prophetic existence", starting at 1.3 billion Fons. The Appraiser sensed fluctuations unlike anything they knew, extremely strong and unstable. A young girl bid 1 Fons and froze the entire hall with the anomaly "Cheese". She let the gavel fall, then walked out the front door, leaving a single coin behind. Hotori was unaffected and freed the Appraiser and the Sterry crew, later admitting it was her doing.

The thief, later identified as Poinsette, had also left the lockpicking anomaly Picky to open the containment devices in the Century Collection Room. That woke Nantanì, Ebisu's security Rule Anomaly: if a lot leaves before it is sold, the venue locks into a closed loop until it is recovered, and nothing from outside can break its rules. Nantanì protects legitimate guests, so the team lost that protection when Pay's copies expired and had to re-contain the breached lots themselves. One of them was Outside the Inner Door, which erodes real space with the spiraling thoughts of writers and would have carved Hethereau apart within nine months. The others were a darkness anomaly and the Class V Never-ending Arachne, which they found waltzing in the Splendid Banquet Hall. Afterwards, Ebisu tried to arrest them for forgery. Jiuyuan countered that Ebisu had privately held a Class V anomaly the Bureau would love to hear about. When Ebisu blamed the thief, Hotori threatened to tear the place apart if they kept talking. Jenson paid Eibon with the lots Hotori had "bought", out of his personal account.

Hotori later admitted she had come to verify something about Sterry and the target ("only half right") and told the Appraiser that Sterry is safe to work with as long as she isn't around. "My dear treasure, wearing your heart on your sleeve might not win you any fans." Elsewhere, unseen schemers reviewed the night. The auction had been bait to bring Sterry and Eibon, Hotori and "that special Esper" included, into contact with the lot, and Ebisu had dared to sell "items related to the prophet". They judged Nightingale sharp and the aloof "witch" best avoided, and as they saw it, the only choice left was "which side of Fraxinus to stand on". The Scarlet Letter later claimed the theft.

8.comment: S1 Ep5 · Dreamwalk Corridor (Part 1: Sunward Resort)
8.content:
**S1 Ep5 · Dreamwalk Corridor (Part 1: Sunward Resort)**
After the Eternal Present case the Bureau held Daffodill for questioning about her Scarlet Letter past, and Director Alphard ordered Eibon not to interfere. Hotori disliked it but understood ("This isn't something one person or one organization can deal with anymore."). Nanally, convinced she had caused her master's injury, grew more miserable by the day. Taygedo won a limited family ticket package to Sunward Resort and gave it to her as "a tribute from your lackey", so the Appraiser took her there to clear her head.

Sunward Resort is a charity house on its own island, funded by the city and managed by the Bureau, where Bio anomalies are rescued and sheltered (dangerous, hard-to-control ones go to the Celaeno Compound) until they find guarantors and can integrate. The famous philanthropist Inanna sponsored the promotion. Iroi, a gentle volunteer guide who wrote everything down in her notes, showed them around the recreation area and the aquatic zone, as well as an ecology farm that had been Lady Inanna's idea. Among the residents were the lucky Noros, elegant and demure, with Inanna as its guarantor, and the Twisties, tiny aquatic anomalies that share memories across any distance and crave cookie crumbs. Bonzita the goldfish has a seven-second memory, and the Wakey Bee collects drowsiness. The shy Flatty and the flammable Fluffy lived there, too, and so did the noisy RABBA RABBA and the garlic-feathered bird Alio Aio ("Just let it go"). Danzaburou and Misty never stop fighting. Nanally was too young to be a guarantor, so Inanna appeared in person and invented a "future guarantor agreement" on the spot, brushing Iroi aside as "a volunteer, not a paid staff member". Nanally chose a little bear-shaped anomaly she felt she had known long ago and named it "Boss Tiger"; to the Appraiser, it looked like a teddy bear ("This girl familiar, like I met before. Me likey.").

At the pier, Daffodill appeared beside the Scarlet Letter girl Poinsette ("Don't come closer.") and left with her through a portal. Poinsette said she had taken The First Branch "fair and square when everyone was watching" and added, "I'm not the one who lured your master away. Am I right, sister?" Nanally spiraled ("Why am I so weak?"), clashed with Sakiri ("The Nanally I knew would never think like this. You don't believe in your master.") and shut herself in her room. Adler revealed that only Hotori had known Daffodill's past ("Since she never told us, we never asked."). The next morning, Nanally was gone, along with the ticket package. Sakiri declared, "Screw the orders."

At the Witch's House, Blackbird divined fog and distant waves calling like irresistible voices. She also saw a half-enclosed giant crisscrossed with fissures and warned that "things aren't what they seem". The resort had no guarantor record under Nanally's name. Hotori reported that missing people across the city had all suffered a recent setback before vanishing, and that some came back oddly cheerful with no memory. The "Boss Tiger" was a Teehee Bear, a vengeful variant of the Cuddly Bear, the playmate anomaly of childhood. Adults see a teddy where children see what they long for, and Teehee Bears deceive the children who forgot them. It had followed Nanally home and watched her break before promising to take her to her master ("A kind woman told me about this secret place."). Everyone defeated it together, and then, a dense fog swallowed the Appraiser.

9.comment: S1 Ep5 · Dreamwalk Corridor (Part 2: The Corridor of Echoes)
9.content:
**S1 Ep5 · Dreamwalk Corridor (Part 2: The Corridor of Echoes)**
The fog led into the Corridor of Echoes, an Anomalous Realm where a ferry sails on land under a sun that neither rises nor sets, while a giant cracked colossus looms over the sea. Its creator, Thyme, a girl with closed eyes, told the Appraiser that they had no dreams to walk and did not belong. People there follow instinct over rules, she said, and the "Dreamwalkers" cast their baggage into the sea to revel in dreams of the past while the procession moves backward. Nanally had become "Nana Tiger", a pink tiger mascot running from everything.

In a garden, the Appraiser met a girl who felt strangely familiar: the dream-self of young Daffodill. She spoke of her archaeologist parents, and of a little sister who shared her room. Then, her memories turned to a "Mother" with many eyes who locked her in a dark room for every mistake, and to the woman she had been sure she killed ("That absolute unkillable demon pursues me relentlessly. She's never ever going to take anyone from me again."). She gave the Appraiser a kaleidoscope that reveals illusions and left: "There are still things I need to do. Goodbye, appraiser." Elsewhere, Inanna warned Daffodill that two of her companions would be stuck forever unless she acted, because "some flowers blossom further after their branches are broken."

Through Nanally's dream sketchbooks, the Appraiser learned her past. As a little girl, she had Boss Tiger, a Cuddly Bear only she could see, who fought tiger gangsters with her like in "Nini's Adventures", and her friends called her a liar for it. When she lost the blue badge he gave her, she chased it across rooftops until she stepped onto a power line and her ability awakened. Boss Tiger told her "this is called growing up" before he faded, since Cuddly Bears nullify themselves as their child grows. Her first Coluccis moved away, too, and then came the day she kicked in Eibon's door and found a family. The real Boss Tiger appeared in her dream to help bring "the real Nanally" out. Nanally confessed that her badge was only a bottle cap and that she feared her urge to protect was fake: "People keep leaving me. Mom, Dad, Boss Tiger, my family members, Master, and maybe you, too." The Appraiser answered that what mattered was the authenticity of her heart.

Thyme would only let a copy leave, a Nanally stripped of obsession and future heartbreak. The Corridor was Thyme's projection, enforced by the Helm of Theseus so that every boat sails only into the past. The Appraiser argued that time must flow forward ("One cannot step into the same river twice.") and fought her, and Thyme's grief broke open: she was the lone survivor of the village of Elvinville and could not understand why she lived. The Appraiser told her to carry that question into other people's lives and to build a tomb for her family where the sun rises. Then, Daffodill struck and nullified Thyme's projection. Inanna stepped through and revealed herself as the Scarlet Letter's leader. Taking the Helm of Theseus, she gloated that she had rigged the ticket win and planted the Teehee Bear. She told Thyme that she had gotten her whole village killed and claimed that Daffodill had grown "bored of playing house" and come home. Zankou sneered at the Appraiser. Inanna let Daffodill spare "that little dreamwalking tiger" and announced, "The game is about to begin." The Dreamwalkers vanished and the Corridor collapsed. The Appraiser escaped with Nanally and Thyme with help from the Twisties, but Nanally had kept only half her soul and fell into a deep sleep.

Mint found them by following the Appraiser's Chuppa ("Coco!"). Sakiri told the sleeping Nanally, "I owe you an apology. I won't allow you to refuse it. Just wake up already." Hotori said the choice was Nanally's ("All of us have absolute agency"). After taking a coded call ("The moth has flown away." "The gardener has been deployed."), she explained that Thyme is a Dimension Visitor, an antique astrolabe anomaly that took the face and name of her last contracted partner. Iroi sent Nanally a hand-sewn pink tiger plush, and the Appraiser promised her a beach day at Cape Dome once she woke.

10.comment: S1 Ep6 · Fogden Game (Part 1: Into the Fog)
10.content:
**S1 Ep6 · Fogden Game (Part 1: Into the Fog)**
More than ten days after the Corridor, Nanally still slept, mumbling about THE WHOOTS!!!! and deals at the docks. Taygedo built her a "Wakey, Wakey, Nanally" clock, and Sakiri sat by her bed because nobody fought her for food anymore. Hotori left a note telling everyone to look after the shop, and the Appraiser found her on the beach with Adler. The truth came out. Daffodill's strike in the Corridor had executed Director Alphard's special containment protocol, which contained the anomaly and moved every Dreamwalker into a safe realm so they would only appear to perish, even in Madam T's eyes; without it, Inanna would have nullified the Corridor with Nanally inside. The Appraiser's interference had changed the boat's course and Thyme's mind, something the protocol could never do. Hotori took the blame ("I am the one who is truly responsible for everything."), and Adler reflected that all children grow up, even "the young head of the household who held everything together just by herself". Alphard's message arrived: "The ant's nest is bustling with commotion. The game is about to begin. The gardeners must act." The gardeners were Eibon and the ETD, joined by Thyme. Hotori warned the Appraiser to steer clear of the Director's "sketchy hacks".

The Scarlet Letter's hideout was the abandoned staff dormitory of a bankrupt company, where an ETD team had lost contact and dozens of visitors had gone in without coming out. Inanna's late-night broadcasts recruited the desperate ("Come, push open the door, enter the Fogden! I, Inanna, shall grant you rebirth."). Inside, a giant tree with tangled roots served as the building's security anomaly. Red lines ran to old CRT televisions that had to be switched off, and a full-length mirror revealed the space's true layout. There, an upright black coffin waited: the Fog Coffin, the Rule Anomaly that destroyed Thyme's village about two hundred years ago, when Inanna alone walked out of its game. Three stolen anomalies had been fed to it, the Helm of Theseus along with the Eternal Present and The First Branch. Over the Chuppa, Alphard cited "educated guesses from Fraxinus" about an unmatched anomaly able to dominate other anomalies, with the power to devour and replicate them as well. On the floor, four red words read past, present, future and liberation. Arresting Madam T would only delay the game a few years, since powerful guests protected her. Alphard handed Chaos full authority on site ("As for Eibon, I believe in Hotori."), and Chaos carried Thyme's true form, the astrolabe, as an escape route.

The Fogden's rules: "Welcome, sinners. Hunt the others, take their Lumen Circles. Ten circles light up the path." Anyone without ten turns to stone and stays forever, and the moon reddens as time runs out.
- The Past (Daffodill, Chaos and Thyme): Daffodill, still the Night Mothling to Chaos, revealed that her return to the Scarlet Letter had been an undercover deal with Alphard, and that her own goal now was "I'm going to kill Madam T." She knocked out the bird-collecting assassin Sweeper instead of killing her ("It's not too late for you.") and beat the former hunters Glaire and Phear (Glaire's eye contract from Inanna had already expired). After the disgraced Scholar fused with an anomaly, she defeated him as well, and later, she refused to drug a kidnapped Esper girl into fake calm ("Painful awareness is better than fake peace."). Monte Cristo, who had sacrificed everything to play, was the one she killed. Zankou ambushed her disguised as Chaos and then as Nanally ("What color am I in your eyes right now?"), and they fought to ritual verses ("Let today be our end of the world, just us two."). Badly hurt, Zankou vanished after moving the kidnapped children to a safe corner. Daffodill claimed the Helm of Theseus, which would let every Dreamwalker, Nanally included, return whole, and Thyme forgave her.
- The Present (Linko, Nitsa and Xiaozhen): they crossed a valley ruled by the giant snake oddity Cavey Snakey (Xiaozhen hates snakes) and found a dead contestant's note ("Kill Inanna and end the game. Fogden will consume everyone's flesh, blood, bone, and souls."). In the room of the Eternal Present, they forgot their own names until a word-chain game brought them back. Inside, they found Adler trapped as a little boy who had to "go to the Tsukinokis" and give "her" something at a certain time, and they freed him.

11.comment: S1 Ep6 · Fogden Game (Part 2: The Future & the Fall of Madam T)
11.content:
**S1 Ep6 · Fogden Game (Part 2: The Future & the Fall of Madam T)**
The Future (the Appraiser): "The nameless ones spin their futures in the fog." The Appraiser walked through possible futures. In one, three months on, headlines screamed "BAC Director Resigns! Dozens Missing!" and Sakiri and Edgar had left to bring the missing home. Taygedo was studying philosophy to learn how to fix bad endings. In another, a century later, the Appraiser ran Eibon alone as the game's sole winner, waiting for souls on the far shore, a future they rejected ("How is it a good ending if I'm the only one left at Eibon?"). In a happy future, everyone smiled and Daffodill promised never to leave, until the Appraiser noticed they were missing from it. Poinsette had been opening doors and speaking through them to show futures from The First Branch, which had never been wrong. In none of them could she find a future in which she survived ("Mother intends to sacrifice everyone for the sake of this game."). The Appraiser spared her and explained why strangers mattered: "That barren concept once known to me as 'home' is now bustling with the people of Eibon. A drunk Shopkeeper, a capable butler, a reliable bodyguard, a noisy handy-otter, and three adorable young employees. I don't want to lose any of them." When she said nobody would remember her, the Appraiser offered to be that person before going on to find The First Branch.

In the arena, Inanna welcomed her "honored guests" and revealed the prize. Hotori was "Eibon's most precious treasure", ageless, with "a power that transcends time itself", and the Fog Coffin's single victor may claim any one thing in the Fogden, even an Esper ability; bound by the three artifacts, Hotori was powerless inside. Inanna meant to feed the Coffin her guests and her "daughters", raised as flowers to nourish her, and to claim "true immortality, more perfect than the Eternal Present". As Champion T she fought with the Fog Coffin's power, and the Fogwraith Colossus rose from the rules. Then, Code Zero appeared ("No! Impossible!"). Inanna transformed into the Amber Broodmother, body and soul lost to the anomaly ("Daffodil, Mommy is here. Your eyes, your life, all belong to me!"), and Zankou turned on her: "Like I said, Daffodill is mine!" Code Zero destroyed the Colossus without effort, and as the Fogden collapsed, it attacked everyone until the Ship of Theseus tore through the sky and took them aboard. Hotori stopped Code Zero's pursuit with a single strike. Chaos reported a confirmed kill on Inanna. "Ashes to ashes, dust to dust."

Aftermath: the Appraiser slept for three days and woke in the dormitory surrounded by everyone, Nanally fully recovered; a woman with closed eyes had walked her along a beach to a shining exit. Daffodill apologized to each of them, to Nanally ("I've been a pretty terrible master") and to Hotori, who had least wanted her to go back yet let her choose ("Freedom is something I learned to appreciate only after joining Eibon."). The chain of tearful sorries ended with the Appraiser: "Sorry, I love you all. We, the people of Eibon, will stay together." Hotori's ability was about 99 percent recovered with two more weeks to go, and the Bureau's compensation let Eibon close for a month. Thyme gave up the Helm of Theseus in exchange for her freedom and stayed at Eibon ("Eibon will be my first harbor. The sun has risen, and the sailors are about to set sail."). Edgar relayed Fraxinus's conclusion that the Fog Coffin was a high-level Rule Anomaly enforcing its rules with absolute power. Zankou went to Ghroth Island with an extensive record. Poinsette, who had pushed the unconscious guests through a door to the Bureau's entrance and then surrendered, was placed at the Esper Academy under supervision, to face trials and later choose between ordinary citizenship and Bureau service. In the Director's office, Alphard explained that Madam T had been "nothing but a pawn of the Fog Coffin", and that a winner only ever received copies duplicated by the Coffin. Code Zero, she added, had shattered a Rule Anomaly the Bureau could only stall. The Appraiser wondered whether Code Zero's real target had been them, and Alphard warned that anyone frightened of Code Zero, or hungry for its power, might tie it to them: "Appraiser, you'll have to be careful."

12.comment: S1 Ep8 · The Witch (Part 1: Starfall Bay)
12.content:
**S1 Ep8 · The Witch (Part 1: Starfall Bay)**
Blackbird received a letter signed "Merula" saying that only Blackbird could handle this commission and that she should come as soon as possible on a boat that would be arranged for her. It didn't name any place and Blackbird's own divination showed nothing. Yggash Court found nothing strange about it, either. The Court preferred that Blackbird stays home and waits for Oracle Stones to come to her, so Lavinia hired the Appraiser privately ("Blackbird can take this chance to leave this cozy cage known as the Witch's House. It's been hundreds of years since she perched on the branch of Fraxinus."). Under the contract, the Appraiser became Blackbird's temporary guardian, tethered to her so that they felt her emotions and shared her burning pain, the way Lavinia does. Blackbird packed lucky charms: a crystal ball to finish a trending anime on and a "maestro-blessed" bracelet, plus a jar of paper cranes and a Fortune Shades prayer plaque she never hung because she wasn't sure what to wish for. She forgot all her luggage anyway. Flying to the meeting point as a bird, she rode there perched on the Appraiser's shoulder, which she declared "wide, comfy, and looks cool".

The boat had nobody at the wheel and sailed into thick fog despite a sunny forecast, bringing them to Starfall Bay, a seaside spot with a cheap hostel and a tree that had gone viral on Bagel. Valmona, a girl who had once visited the Witch's House, was hiding because everyone else was murmuring about fire trials for witches. Tourists who came for the viral tree photo had been trapped for days by a fog that prickled and numbed, voting on witches like a party game while chanting their wishes ("Burn the witch and pass the bar exam"). ETD Squad 4's Skia and Fadia were already investigating. Fadia had been burned at a ritual and laughed it off ("It's not my first ritual or execution."), and she teased the Appraiser for always turning up where there's danger "like a puppy with a sharp nose". Skia explained witch-hunting anomalies: they are born when extreme collective fear makes a group lose its reason and hunt for a culprit, they amplify that fear and destroy outcasts first, and they are nullified by removing fear and restoring reason. Modern ones grow from online rumours and fade once the truth comes out, while one as strong as this Inquisitor ("I am the Inquisitor sent by the Highest. The fire of the Highest One cleanses all sin.") belonged to the far past. People it burned turned into Oracle Stones while their bodies slept, and something was blocking Blackbird from guiding their souls.

When the sacred tree caught fire and the stones shook with souls crying for help, Blackbird walked into the flames ("Don't be afraid. I'm here."), and the Appraiser followed her.

13.comment: S1 Ep8 · The Witch (Part 2: St. Arbor)
13.content:
**S1 Ep8 · The Witch (Part 2: St. Arbor)**
They woke up centuries in the past in the town of St. Arbor, where the herbalist Annie, who looked exactly like Valmona, mistook them for injured runaway serfs and hid them from constables who would call them consorts of the devil. Plague, flood, famine, drought and a lost war had left the land desperate as a Confessor blamed pacts with the devil, and the nearby village of Casco had already been razed. Annie warned that diviners are the first suspected of witchcraft, so Blackbird must never divine in public. This is when we get to know Magistrate Victor: he was devout and strict, needing to take care of his ill wife Martha. In the town hall, scarecrows hung "for warding off evil" on the sacred tree where Saint Arbor once prayed for rain. Then, the Inquisitor Cotton Hathorne arrived, declared the town cursed by a witch and began trials. The girl Abigail and her friends acted possessed and named witches. Lizzie Corey, widow of Pickett Corey, who died trying to save Mary, was burned ("If you take my life, the Highest One will give you blood to drink.") and became an Oracle Stone. Blue flames in the Inquisitor's eyes marked the anomaly taking shape. Blackbird's memories blurred until she believed she was a townsperson.

The greedy constable Billy Putnam, who had swindled his neighbours out of land and let his own brother die, threatened Annie and demanded she marry him. Annie turned the trial against him with every family's secrets, and once the girls named Billy, he was burned. Crushed by guilt, Annie resolved to confess as the witch, and Blackbird, now calling herself "Merula the vagabond", offered to die in her place. The truth surfaced: "Annie" was Merula, and Blackbird was the price Merula had paid "the devil", half of her soul, eventually becoming her own person. Long ago, Merula stepped forward as the witch to save everyone, and when she beheld the Inquisitor in the fire, she cursed it with all her pain; her Esper ability awakened in the flames at the cost of half her soul, which flew away as a spark among birds. Everyone in St. Arbor died anyway, Annie included, while Merula's power formed the Fleshbound Cage, a hell for St. Arbor's people and a cage that preserved the anomaly through time. As her power waned, the Inquisitor broke out at Starfall Bay, so she sent the letter and posed as Valmona and as Annie to make Blackbird remember.

The Appraiser refused to leave without Blackbird and anchored her with her own memories, from the crystal-ball anime and the lucky charms to Lavinia and the brave tourists. "Please, forever remember that you are not Merula. You are Blackbird." Blackbird answered, "I was once Merula from St. Arbor. And now I am Blackbird of the Witch's House. We are each other's lost half soul." Destroying the realm would release the Inquisitor into modern Hethereau, which cannot sustain it, so they broke the Fleshbound Cage and defeated it ("Burning witches won't make things better and won't stop the madness. Merula, you can rest."). Merula said goodbye ("For we are the unburning witches."), and the Appraiser told her that the sunrise in Hethereau is beautiful. For the first time, Blackbird cleansed the Oracle Stones without pain, with a blessing: "Nightmares shall not come. All bitterness shall cease. Forget every sorrow, every fright, and dream a dream of peace."

Outside, only ten minutes had passed. Skia would file a detailed report on a rare nullification of a witch-hunting anomaly, and the JTF would send the red Oracle Stones to the Witch's House, though Fadia wished she could keep them. Blackbird renamed her hat "Merula". Lavinia gave the Appraiser a new commission to plan an itinerary and show Blackbird the city ("I just realized how wonderful Hethereau is. For Merula's sake, too."), which began with an amusement park and a merry-go-round. Since then, Blackbird has sent the Appraiser an invitation of her own.

key: Meet Me in the Data Stream
14.comment: S1 Ep9 · Meet Me in the Data Stream (Part 1: The Invalid Number)
14.content:
**S1 Ep9 · Meet Me in the Data Stream (Part 1: The Invalid Number)**
Late one night at Eibon, Edgar ended a long call with a school friend he had fallen out with and not heard from in two years; the friend had called because the "invalid number" was trending on Bagel again, a topic they used to argue about. Edgar told the Appraiser the legend. About four years ago, a Bagel user dreamed that a blurry, long-lost friend recited a phone number and asked to be called. The number was invalid, yet soon strangers all over the world reported the same dream and the same digits, until the story faded after a year. His friend thought someone had made it up; Edgar thought it was a meme anomaly, the kind ordinary containment cannot touch. Out of curiosity, the Appraiser dialed it and heard "The number you have dialed is not in service", noting the digits 316651 before going to bed. They woke on a soft, clean carpet, unsure whether this was a dream or an anomalous realm. A locked phone on the floor rang, and a worried voice said, "Are you doing okay there? I couldn't get in touch. I was worried about you." It was Nitsa, and the Appraiser told her she had the wrong number.

At the Bureau, Linko said Nitsa's frequencies were full of static, and Chaos gave the Appraiser "oral authorization from me and Tiny" to visit ETD-6's office on the 17th floor. Behind its security-coded door, Nitsa explained that the phone belonged to her best friend, the squad's lieutenant, who always answered at once and had been silent for over a month. Before leaving, the captain and lieutenant had worked overtime sorting intel and left Chaos a wanted list long enough to keep him busy for three months, and he had already caught everyone on it. The captain told Chaos and Linko he was dealing with a high-class anomaly, while the lieutenant told Nitsa they had business on Ghroth Island tied to "an ongoing anomaly murder case". Ghroth Island has no signal, though, and the call had connected. Nitsa chose to break the rules and hired the Appraiser privately, making sure nobody else would be blamed ("wanting to help a friend is what made me join the bureau in the first place"). When a call rang through on the squad's work phone and Nitsa answered it, only the Appraiser was pulled in.

The realm was a glowing building of data made of archive units, each holding one person's memories of a friendship. In the first, a man and his neighbor across the hall shared dinners until the neighbor, who loved the man's carpet, moved away; in the version the anomaly built for him, the neighbor came back laid off and divorced to the same cheap apartment, ready to be friends again. A voice over a speaker guided the Appraiser ("You're on the right track") and unlocked the door: Exe, ETD-6's captain, who recognized "Variable Z" from their profile. He apologized for worrying people outside and explained that the lieutenant was fine, the phone being a spare. Then, he briefed them. The invalid number had grown from a harmless Class I meme anomaly into a Class VI anomaly, the Imaginary Old Friend, which rebuilds estranged friends from stolen memory data until the real friend is replaced (see "World BG · Imaginary Old Friend"), and he was cracking its storage media one by one to find its core. When the Appraiser released a school-festival memory and the curly, blue-haired lieutenant from Nitsa's photo stepped out, Exe cut Nitsa's link to the realm ("I nuked your login, variable Z"). The Appraiser woke somewhere else.

They were in a bright rift outside the realm, under a looping sky, where pixel flowers and grass covered hills that ended in an invisible wall. A silver-haired girl helped them up and said that if nobody named her, she went by Elyms. She was the Imaginary Old Friend itself, and the rift was a cell built by someone's wish to make something last forever. From chat logs and recordings, the Appraiser worked out whose it was: a boy and a friend who lived inside a computer, who had named him "the unknown X". It belonged to Exe. Elyms then explained her pact with The Circle and her single identity as ETD-6's lieutenant. Each of Nitsa, Linko and Chaos sees her in a different form, she said, and she told the Appraiser why they had not been able to see her at all. Exe had been assigned to work with her three years ago and killed her the day he understood her. Now, he had taken leave to nullify her for good, unconcerned about Ghroth Island or his future. She told how the real Roxanne had abandoned Nitsa and how Exe had forced through the call that let Elyms take her place. Then, she offered the Appraiser a long call over a paper cup phone and a story.

15.comment: S1 Ep9 · Meet Me in the Data Stream (Part 2: The Elf in a Shell)
15.content:
**S1 Ep9 · Meet Me in the Data Stream (Part 2: The Elf in a Shell)**
Elyms streamed the session to her "off-site supervisor", who allowed it ("whatever") and cut in whenever her version of his life drifted. Boy X was a friendless, bad-tempered prodigy who found an abandoned PC disconnected from the internet in a storage room and picked its lock to make it his secret base. A program he could not delete lived inside: Y, "the incredible Elf in a Shell", who claimed to be an Esper who had turned into data for a long nap. X ran antivirus scans and went as far as reformatting and reinstalling, yet Y kept saying, "Let's play. Come by anytime." For six years, they played every night, and Y pranked him all the way even as she skipped levels and opened doors for him like picking "green peppers off a kid's plate". As X grew up, Y pushed him to think about school and his future out in the world, and he refused ("As long as I have you and this PC, we can go to any world we want"). The PC was dying. One evening, a crash ate his save, and when Y gently suggested he should go out and find something fun, X typed "This is all your fault, you virus", passing up three chances to stop and sending it while Y was still typing. Y locked him out. He drafted an apology and threw it away. Coming back at 23:31, he waited for Y to apologize first while Y peeked at the chat window every fifty seconds. At 23:50, he imagined reaching into the data like "the hand of Y" to forge a game weapon. As his favorite character, a free and indomitable marksman, he would crack the box open and free Y. The box opened onto a blue screen and an explosion as if from invisible bullets, and X was left bleeding with a gun pulled out of a game in his hand. He never apologized. The Bureau found no victim, and nobody could prove Y had ever existed.

In that memory, the Appraiser saw Y's portrait, an elf with a mouse cursor hairpin, and Elyms looked just like it. She admitted that overwriting his memories of Y was the hardest job she had ever tried, and that he had refused even a dream in which Y apologized first. Asked which Y was more real, the remembered one or the regenerated one, the Appraiser would not choose. As an ideal friend, she could not fight back or call for help, so she had pulled in a stranger: either Exe would have to come back for the witness, or the witness would change something. The Appraiser offered to be her friend as she was, and they played games together.

Meanwhile, Exe read every corner of the realm and poured it all into his own head, finding the real Elyms among 316,650 clones ("Found you."). The Appraiser came back to find him standing empty over his "murder" and argued that the friendships she gave 310,000 people were real, even if the memories were not. Exe had understood that three years ago and fought the Appraiser anyway, far past his limits, until he destroyed all 316,650 connections at once and the realm began to crash. Calls from the people who rely on her, a friend demanding a treat for a missed school festival and an elderly friend asking whether the rain had set off an old backache among them, pieced her back together, and she rewrote her code with broader permissions. Taking the Appraiser's offhand idea that a friend can also be an enemy, she decided Exe needed her as one. She sent the Appraiser home through a ringing phone booth and fought him herself, a match that ended in an old chat window: "Let's play tomorrow, Y!" "See ya, X!"

Back in Hethereau, the Appraiser left Nitsa a message through a Chuppa. Days later, Elyms called them to the Bureau's server room, a network space of floating screens, her projection glitching like a body with every bone broken. Her realm was in ruins and Exe had passed out after weeks of three- or four-hour nights of trying to nullify her; a trial looked unlikely, since it would expose her and cost the ETD two members. She described the squad's secret tug-of-war and thanked "Variable Z" as the first total stranger to become her friend, though she warned that she will still patch the memories of anyone who wavers. Chaos and Linko were told the pair needed a hospital stay, and Linko read "the kind of frequencies you get when people pretend they're getting along". When Exe stirred in a dark data space, Elyms told him he had lost this round and that she still holds the blurred memory of the last second before the blue screen, the key back to his goodbye with Y, as "the bonus loot you'll get when you kill the enemy boss. Go earn it." He answered, "Challenge accepted," and they went back to a mountain of reports. Asked whether he was ready to return to this world, Exe said, "Same as always."

16.content:
**S1 Spinoff · Pawn Moonlight**
Bianca, public relations manager of the luxury brand Landric, hired Eibon under strict and expensive confidentiality to find Toshi, the genius perfumer who had vanished while developing a new product line. His pristine flat in the Eden Apartments came with a lab and a zen garden, and even the recipes on his fridge were gram-exact. There, a strange bird and a dog stole his incense burner from under the team's noses. Jiuyuan of Sterry Express pointed them to Cake Sweeper, author of the hit manga "Tales of Nil", who first tried to drive them off thinking they were her editors. Outside her door waited Boomboom, a young man who had recognized his long-lost dog Dandelion in her latest chapter, and in the commotion Kiroumaru swallowed Dandelion's collar, Boomboom's only keepsake. Cake Sweeper explained that her success came from Pawn Moonlight, where any wish could be granted for the right price, and that the dog and bird in her manga lived there. At the Moby-Dick Bookstore, a disguised stranger slipped past everyone except the Appraiser, who saw his true young face.

Next the chef Kenneth, head cook of the restaurant Delichemy, hired Eibon through Hyelp, claiming the pawnshop's owner had taken his sense of taste "without reason" and pointing them to Green Wall Slope. The team spoke their wishes together under the moon, and the giant door opened. The owners were twin brothers, the cold and formal Mismo (the stranger from the bookstore) and his relaxed brother Otro, wandering Espers who had lived there for six months as guests of the realm's true master: the dog Dandelion, in truth the Class IV spatial anomaly Morphix (profile U-5228). Sakiri clashed with Mismo on the upper platforms, and when she started beating Kiroumaru to make him cough up the collar, Morphix's distress transformed him into a huge winged white wolf that fought the team. Boomboom arrived on the battlefield, and the monster instantly became a happy dog licking his owner's face.

The truth came out. Kenneth had pawned ten years of his sense of smell for a career-making kitchen knife, then stacked a second contract on the same knife, giving up his sense of taste for life to win a star in the culinary guide La Palourde Blanche; when the knife's power ran out, he still owed both prices. He had dragged his friend Toshi to the pawnshop ("No pain, no gain"), and Toshi had traded twenty years of his sense of smell for a historic fragrance in the incense burner, then never lit it, choosing his own hard work over a shortcut. When Toshi decided to return it and cancel, Kenneth kidnapped him to keep his own plans hidden and hired Eibon to destroy the realm and void his debts. Toshi's open contract had been draining Otro's lifespan, so Mismo went looking for him and rescued him. Waiting safely at the realm's summit, Toshi told everyone the twins had saved his life. Adler invoked clause six on page two of the commission contract (client deception means the full fee and a forfeited deposit) and invoiced Kenneth, having already notified the Bureau. Kenneth screamed that he would sue them all and was arrested. Hotori felt uneasy cashing Landric's final payment, since she adores their skincare.

The twins asked Eibon to keep their business secret and left Hethereau to find a way to stabilize Otro's fading life. Before going, they gave Sakiri a keepsake, a small box with shifting designs holding little bears made to look like the Eibon members ("Everything in this pawn shop has its destined owner. You no longer have to sign any contracts."); her wish had been "I hope that I will find a place where I belong and it won't abandon me." Boomboom applied to become Morphix's guarantor, and Pawn Moonlight vanished from Green Wall Slope.

17.comment: S1 Spinoff · Tomato Jelly Rampage: Live Report!
17.content:
**S1 Spinoff · Tomato Jelly Rampage: Live Report!**
Taygedo grabbed a bounty to debunk the urban legend of the "Tomato Devil", an anomaly smashing Tomato 100 tomato-jelly vending machines, and rival hunters claimed the Devil was Lacrimosa of ETD Squad 4. Mint found "Lacrimosa senpai" napping ("Five more minutes") and explained over Blizzi ice cream. Lacrimosa had once tried to buy tomato jelly by lifting and shaking a vending machine ("Is that not the way?"). Skia paid the compensation and made her apologize, but passers-by posted photos. At first, people found her endearing; then, someone revealed she was ETD, and the comments turned vicious with claims of privilege abuse and Bureau cover-ups while the facts were ignored. The hatred on Bagel condensed into a Meme Anomaly that looked like her and acted out the rumours, which fed the rumours further. An obsessed photographer risked their life near fights to snap her. The higher-ups put her on temporary leave, and Bureau experts recommended letting it blow over. Mint couldn't accept that.

Adler explained that meme anomalies are tied to collective perception, so brute force means nothing and the only cure is weakening the shared belief, which takes time. The Appraiser's plan used Taygedo's Bagel account, banned from posting but still able to livestream: they would broadcast the real Lacrimosa fighting the Tomato Devil. Lacrimosa agreed once promised "a lot a lot a lot of tomato jelly" ("Hold on tight, television." "Swifter than the breeze."). The stream flipped the conversation, and the Devil weakened and dissolved into tomato jelly. Skia arrived after work and apologized formally, calling the repair of public damage part of the Bureau's duty to the city. Then, she taught Lacrimosa to thank everyone ("Thank you, appraiser. Thank you, Taygedo." "Thank you, doggo."). By the next day, the internet had moved on to Ellie Cordelein's doll project "Thousand Faces", and Taygedo sulked over the lost spotlight. Adler: "Whether a rumor simply fades away or is properly dispelled, for those involved, the difference is immense."

18.comment: S1 Spinoff · Where Words Sprout, Fall Unfolds
18.content:
**S1 Spinoff · Where Words Sprout, Fall Unfolds**
A worried couple asked Eibon to find their son Maiyue, who had vanished after school. He is a quiet boy from White Parrot Street who struggles to speak and is uncomfortable with strangers, though he brings fresh flowers home every week. Eibon only takes anomaly-related work, Adler noted, but it accepted the job to reassure the family and sent the Appraiser alone. The trail ran from Hillside Blooms and the Moby-Dick Bookstore through Clement Academy's Garden Club to the abandoned manor of the Serenetti family, who owned it centuries ago; their descendant lives outside Hethereau, beyond the reach of the Bureau's Intercity Affairs Department. Baicang and Skia were already there investigating abnormal Wertheimer fluctuations, and Baicang joined the Appraiser while whining that Skia should bring a gurney to carry him back. Skia: "I see you still remember who you are. Good."

In the hall, Fleur the Storyteller narrated the Serenetti master's poisoned family ("Family bliss. Harmony. Master never allowed us to talk about these things. We want to say it."). In the glass house, the Location Anomaly C-3624 "Silent Garden" was spreading. Its plants served as its limbs and senses and even as its speech, while its pollen carried anger and malice. Maiyue had become its "temporary gardener" and its Nexus, and he spoke on its behalf from among rock roses, the flower of sensitivity and rejection ("Words burst forth like a storm of pollen. I will stay here and live as one with it."). They brought him the bouquet he had meant for his parents. Baicang signed to him in sign language, then needled him hard to provoke a real answer ("So that's how you love them"). At last, he spoke aloud: "Well done. I heard your every word. Now fade at once, nameless being." Every plant withered as if autumn had come early, and the anomaly was nullified. Maiyue lost his voice permanently along with the Nexus but was otherwise unharmed, and he thanked them with handmade flower cards, one addressed "to the big bro with a soothing voice". His parents said that people who care about him will always find the patience to understand him.

Over flower tea, when the Appraiser offered to split the reward, Baicang said he would rather see it as helping a friend. He joked that his power was "plant talk" because he simply asked the plants to wither, and he would not say what he had signed or why he knows sign language. "When you do care about someone, you will always find a way to understand him. So, why don't you try caring for me? My answers might be right here."

19.comment: S1 Spinoff · A Legendary(?) Band's First Page
19.content:
**S1 Spinoff · A Legendary(?) Band's First Page**
Haniel invited the Appraiser to StarSign, a basement livehouse on Fiscus Avenue, where they met the bartender Akane Rin and the owner Kiyosawa. Haniel picked up the guitar she had once taught herself, and with Kiyosawa offering practice space, Nanally proposed forming a band with the Appraiser and Haniel. Akane agreed to mentor them, insisting she was only helping them practice and would never be their vocalist. They rehearsed "Heroic Appearance", "Everlasting Dazing Summer", "Destiny" and "Mayoiuta" and pushed tickets on Tamamochi Street and at Food First. The warm-up debut at StarSign was all nerves and mistakes until Akane stepped in and saved the show.

The next goal was the legendary music festival Night of Moondog, a Location Anomaly where performers score by how strongly they resonate with anomalies. Hoping to "grind XP twice as fast", Haniel and Nanally snuck off to challenge the graffiti anomaly Bopp with music and went missing. The Appraiser and Akane found them, and Akane, who rarely loses her temper, exploded: "Didn't anyone teach you to never underestimate any anomaly? One misstep, just one, and you'd be injured. Then no more hunting, no more music, no more chasing the thing you love most with the people you care about." After apologizing for overreacting, she agreed to street performances and officially joined as lead vocalist. The band took the name THE WHOOTS!!!! ("I'll skip saying the four exclamation marks out loud. Just feel them."), with the Appraiser on drums. They did not win Night of Moondog, scoring 60 points on debut. Afterwards, Akane met Aurelia, her former bandmate from Lines, and the grudge they had carried for years finally eased: "Starlight scatters but never truly disappears."

20.comment: S1 Spinoff · Fighting with a Dragon (999 Nights)
20.content:
**S1 Spinoff · Fighting with a Dragon (999 Nights)**
Weeks after the Fogden, a recovering Nanally tried to climb out of Eibon's window to visit Mint ("healthy as a tiger") and was caught by Adler, who had been gardening nearby. He promised a family party once she healed and sent the Appraiser off with cookies, and Nanally ordered them to have as much fun as possible with no spoilers. At Mint's messy apartment, CSU Squad 2 (Mint, proud to finally be a senpai, the former Sunward volunteer Iroi and the new transfer Shinku) sat down with the Appraiser to play the famous board game "999 Nights", based on the tale of an unlucky fisherman who tells a river god a new story every night for 999 nights to keep its blessing. Its heart is the anomaly toy Dice Lord, which customizes the story for its players and narrates in a borrowed voice. Mint put every point into strength as the Barbarian and got treated by the game as a pet, while Iroi played the Mage and threatened her with silence spells. The Appraiser was the Swordsman, and Shinku drew the Villager, with no class at all.

The game opened on the Warren Continent, where the Fuzzies, sheep-like creatures made of cotton candy who say "baa", had lost their great city Fluffopolis to the Crimson Dragon, which forced them to build it a tower and toasted their bottoms with fiery sneezes. Long ago, a heroine's party had slain or crippled the gold, white, azure and black dragons and forged the Dragon Armor from their trophies. The Elder took Shinku for the heroine or her descendant, and the heroine's untouched room held a level-up candy that Mint fed straight to her. They crossed the Chocolate Volcano and the Milk Ice Mountain, and then the illusory Amber Syrup Lake, which shows each traveler their worst fear. Shinku saw her other self ("I am the real you. The one who loses her mind when using abilities.") and swore never to use her powers again; Mint dreamed of an anomaly printer churning out exam sheets, and Iroi of a flood washing Fuzzies into cotton candy wafers. Mint admitted she had secretly followed Shinku on missions to look out for her. That night, Shinku told the Appraiser about her horns and her temper, and about her fear of dragging the others down: "I'm happy to have met you."

The Mysterious Fuzzy Merchant revealed the real legend. The armor overtakes its wearer whenever they are weak or tired. The heroine lost control and crippled her companions, letting the Crimson Dragon escape, and afterwards, she gave up her strength and shattered the armor across the continent. Mint called that heroine a coward and wanted to rewrite the ending. Iroi promised she could put Shinku to sleep whenever she liked, since even the crankiest dragon becomes a softy after a good nap, and Mint added, "Who cares about you losing control? Bring it on." Shinku put on the armor at Crimson Castle. The dragon faked surrender and mocked her that she would shred her friends, and she briefly lost control ("I don't want to hurt you.") until her friends called her back ("Shinku, you're not alone. Trust us.") and she accepted that side of herself. The Fuzzies now sing of the great Dragonfruit Knight Paya and her three treasured companions. Afterwards, Mint demanded a rematch. An old photo then revealed that Shinku had worked at the Bureau "with Master" ever since her powers awoke, which made her no rookie at all and brought Mint's senpai act crashing down. Mint's cooking remains a hazard.

21.comment: S1 Spinoff · To Us, Back Then
21.content:
**S1 Spinoff · To Us, Back Then**
Clement Academy celebrated its centennial, and after pleas from Haniel and Nanally, Akane returned as a special guest alumna with THE WHOOTS!!!! and most of Eibon in tow. They bought proper school uniforms and Akane brought her old classmate Aurelia to meet the band. On festival day, they met Suzuha, the third member of Lines, who said she was only there for the anniversary: "Us three can't go back to what we were." The stalls were a riot. Besides takoyaki, there was a shooting gallery where Nanally narrated the fall and rise of the Coluccis and a rhythm game that Suzuha dominated. At a memory game, Haniel bragged that elite couriers memorize fifteen addresses at a glance, and Nanally stole Aurelia's fresh cookies straight from the oven. Baicang turned up as Garden Club advisor at Maiyue's invitation and introduced his named plants Tang Yuan, Chuggy, BB and Blanca. He sold Blanca to the Appraiser for 1 Fon, admitting he envies plants for being "silent, but resilient". Blackbird ran a divination booth as "the Puzzler" ("My crystal ball won't show answers to your next test.") and foresaw "someone writing a very long letter" for the three Lines girls. Sinclair and Klingsna Dvořák ran the prize redemption booth, paying Puka Group chocolate coins for stage performances, so THE WHOOTS!!!! signed up. Giovanni Dvořák later opened the festival to the public.

Before the show, Akane told the Appraiser about Lines. Childhood friends Akane, Aurelia and Suzuha played as a band and hunted anomalies, saving the hunter money for venues. When Akane flunked math, Aurelia tutored her, and she always knew where Akane snuck off to practice. Suzuha was the one who raced to the cafeteria to grab lunch for all three. Then, Aurelia was hurt and got paralysed from the waist down forever, which resulted in her family blaming the band and the hunting for the tragic incident. Due to the chaos unfolding, Suzuha moved to another city to run away from her sorrows and Lines ended; Akane typed and deleted every reply to Aurelia's messages and tore up her own songs. The concert was a success. Afterwards, they dug up the time capsule Akane had buried, a DSD POP "Memory Projector" toy derived from a space-time projector anomaly and meant to record graduation day. It had recorded the aftermath instead, and it opened an Anomalous Realm of buried memories. Nanally and Suzuha were thrown back to the day Lines met the anomaly Swallowtail, which cost Aurelia the use of her legs. Suzuha wanted to run, but Nanally told her it would be different this time, and once the others arrived, they defeated Swallowtail together.

Aurelia: "The pain will never end if we run away every time we think about the past. The past is settled. There are no what-ifs." Suzuha admitted that leaving Hethereau never helped. Akane: "Remember why we started our band? We wanted to stay together forever. Let's start all over. I'm Akane Rin. What's your name?" Aurelia replayed their first meeting: "Rin, it sounds like you like music a lot. I'll call you Rinny then." They sang "Letters to me", and the night ended with fireworks and a bonfire party with nearly everyone the Appraiser knows.

22.comment: S1 Side Story · New Anomaly Citizen ID!
22.content:
**S1 Side Story · New Anomaly Citizen ID!**
Not long after Taygedo's failed romance, he and Nanally had a blowout on Eibon's second floor over the tokusatsu show "Kokoro Rider". Nanally, a devoted fan of the legendary hunter Mr. Galaxis who inspired the show, despised its romance-heavy third season; Taygedo defended it because Tako liked it and could only shout "Tayge! Tayge!" (Nanally, no taste!). Edgar recited ratings data and Sakiri revealed suspicious expertise, but Taygedo and Nanally still stormed off on bad terms. That night, Taygedo turned up at Adler's door hugging his pillow, and over a late snack, he asked Adler to take him to renew his Anomaly Citizen ID instead of Nanally. Adler was busy, so Taygedo picked the Appraiser and forgot to tell them. He paid them back with a week of Blizzi ice cream and two weeks of "Weekly Fantasy", and declared a new chapter of otter independence.

At the Bureau, Taygedo bonded instantly with Barracuda over wrenches ("Taygedo, Eibon's chief mechanic!") before handing his papers to Mr. Bag. He posed for a new ID photo in specially chosen clothes that looked exactly like his usual ones and then aced the Safety Assessment Room. Barracuda invited him to join Logistics and told the Appraiser the Woofo Renaming Saga. Taygedo, meanwhile, started giving away his "inheritance" (his Chip-Eating Finger Washer to the Appraiser, chocolate liqueur to "sleepy Hotori", unopened manga to Edgar, Gubichi supplies to Sakiri and his toolbox to Daffodill) so he could become a Bureau hero and the inspiration for the next Kokoro Rider. He wanted his profile number U-5291 changed to a lucky one, and Mr. Bag refused because the format is fixed. At the anomaly staff coffee time, Ms. Fei offered him "Deadline Essential" coffee and cheerfully crushed his dream of joining the ETD. Agent LUCK hoped he would be better with computers than Barracuda, who was dragged off to fix a vending machine on his day off. Taygedo concluded that the Bureau was "super scary".

Then, Nanally texted an apology. Taygedo admitted he had only been stubborn and that he would rather be "Eibon's Taygedo", Eibon's best mechanic, than "Hero Taygedo". His new ID photo made him swear a diet starting tomorrow. Back home, he apologized at full volume, and Nanally forgave him as the Ichi-daime: "A true gangster understands their family, and respects what their family likes too. There can't be any bad blood between the Coluccis!" They planned to binge the first two seasons together. The big clean-up turned up his missing sketchbook, covered in Kiroumaru's bite marks.

23.comment: S1 Side Stories · Hethereau Odd Jobs
23.content:
**S1 Side Stories · Hethereau Odd Jobs**
Smaller cases and encounters the Appraiser has handled around Hethereau, useful as callbacks and recurring faces:
- A Retrograde Poem for You (Miguel District): Puff the Snowman wanted to bring winter early by gathering enough cold air to freeze the city. The Appraiser photographed him promoting Nekomaru Ramen and riding a truck, then posing on the ice sculptures at the Gold Apple Collection Hall and on the Hethereau Skytower rooftop. They also ran deliveries to Clicky, Panda Hotpot and Budoriya, and in the end found only his grass circle by Caltrop Lake. Snow has fallen in Hethereau ever since. Faces: Daisy, Consuelo, Koharu, Nekomaru and Giovanni Dvořák.
- Books Are Like Old Friends (Miguel District): newsstand owner Miles suspected an anomaly in his stand. The trail ran from his teacup to the Surprise Box shop, then by way of Aria and Kilos to JTF members Futaba and Shifan. In the end, a search for Miles himself led from Saint Torres Avenue to the Crazy Cat bubble tea shop and the Miguel District Train Station.
- Drift Away, Legend! (Miguel District): the Novus ST79 outside Natsunari Tofu, the "Midnight Ghost Racer of Hethereau", belonged to the tofu shop's Sota; out-racing his rival Bai Yang twice nullified the anomaly "Don't Stop Me Now!". Mint came along.
- Goodbye, Yellow Flag (Bridge Crossings): the racer Gethrie tried to unload her freshly serviced car "Aurora" for 40,001 Fons, suspiciously fast, and a race against Coastal Drift followed.
- Let's Go, Delicious Investigators! (New Herland): the anomaly Frizzle was upset about how people eat, and after interviews at the Moby-Dick Bookstore and a showdown with the anomaly Danzaburou in an alley, a gift of Clicky Fries made it right. River helped with Joey and Hatsuharu, and Adler texted afterwards.
- Seeing and Believing (Hankaku Street): a mysterious figure was troubling the street's shops. Faces: Violet, Leah, Uncle Prime, Ekko, Grace and Good Joe.
- In the Reflection (Bridge Crossings): a case built around a rumoured magic mirror at the vintage shop, involving a grocery shop owner and a washbasin filled with water.
- Transform! Huhehaha! (Bridge Crossings): an upside-down phone booth led to Mysty, a shapeshifter who leaves clues like "Bzzz", "waka" and "Crunch Crunch".
- We! Are! One! (Bridge Crossings): a talking Oddity and its crowd of friends: Ruddy, Auddy, Buddy, Nydia, Danzaburou, Aubury and Kodak.
- Weather Watch (Bridge Crossings): the Rainmen attacks traced to their cause with Fir, Pluvio, Bixing and May.
- The Records Collector (Bridge Crossings): record-shop owner Sidd's case led past Puka Candy and the Moby-Dick Bookstore, then 9°C Coffee, to music coming from Eibon's own second floor, where Sakiri and Kiroumaru were involved. Faces: Asahi Inori, Dylan and Kesha.
- Fluffed Away?! (Bridge Crossings): calming the anomaly Fluffy with cotton fabric on behalf of Eric's staff.
- Sweet Cakes, Bitter Cakes (Bridge Crossings): free bakery samples with Alice, Eliton, Rabi, Leah and Mr. Bag.
- Taygedo in Big Trouble!: rescuing Taygedo from the Wishing Pool in Nacupeda Park.
