66.content:
**Mismo & Otro** · Twin Caretakers of Pawn Moonlight
Mismo and Otro are wandering Esper twins who drift from city to city "for certain reasons", without roots. For six months, they lived in Pawn Moonlight as guests of its master, the dog anomaly Morphix, whom they call Dandelion; they managed his diet and his shedding anxiety and ran the realm as a pawnshop (see "World BG · Pawn Moonlight"). Twin Espers' powers resonate like magnets, and theirs combined with Morphix's space to grant wishes. They left Hethereau to find a way to stabilize Otro's fading life.

Mismo: serious and disciplined, he keeps to himself and stays formal to the point of distance, with a voice "cold as ice". He apologizes at once for his own mistakes and keeps every relationship strictly businesslike. His ability handles exchange and contracts: he formalizes deals as "Confirmations" and collects their price. He can disguise himself at will so that others see a different person, though the Appraiser always sees his true young face. He threatens lethal force against anyone who endangers Otro. Every shedding season brings him terrible allergies, yet for all his complaining, he will miss Dandelion badly. Otro says he was more straightforward as a child.

Otro: the relaxed, playful twin, whose presence is so faint it feels "like flowing sand". Unpaid contract costs drain his lifespan, so the twins depend on deals being settled. He teases Mismo and translates Mismo's hidden feelings for others. It was Otro who let Cake Sweeper use the realm as manga reference, on condition that neither twin was drawn.

APPEARANCE: The twins look nearly identical, with tousled sky-blue hair, blue eyes and earrings. Both wear white shirts with ruffled jabots and white trousers under long black hooded coats lined in bright blue, with a teal crest on the back. Mismo can disguise himself at will, yet the Appraiser always sees his true, youthful face. Mismo stays formal to the point of distance, with a voice "cold as ice", while Otro is the relaxed twin who translates his brother's hidden feelings for everyone else.

67.content:
**Morphix (Dandelion) & Boomboom**
Morphix, profile U-5228, is a Class IV High-Risk Oddity that rewrites reality to build complex Anomalous Realms, setting their entry and exit conditions and reshaping them at will, which gives him an overwhelming home advantage inside his own realm. His appearance depends on his intent and the observer. Usually he is a fluffy white dog who looks harmless, while inside his realm, he becomes a huge white wolf with wings, presumed to be his true form. Researchers wonder whether he reads minds, and his Nexus is unknown. Rather than contain him, the Bureau's protocol is to stay on good terms with him by meeting his everyday needs, while monitoring him and his guarantor. He reached Hethereau by sneaking onto a cargo ship after a pretty female dog, and he adores his owner. His favourite foods are roasted duck and apple bites, with yogurt besides, and he sheds enough white fur to give people allergies.

Boomboom is the polite, gentle young man who named him Dandelion for the fur that drifts off him like dandelion seeds. Their weekend ritual was a beach walk and a stop at a 24-hour convenience store for treats; the rest of the week Dandelion slept on the rug by the sofa and watched TV series with him. Boomboom lost him while running back to a fast-food restaurant for a forgotten manga and searched for eleven months, guilt-ridden, until he recognized his dog in "Tales of Nil". When Morphix rampaged in Pawn Moonlight, Boomboom's arrival calmed him instantly. He thanked Mismo and Otro for keeping his dog safe and applied to be Morphix's guarantor, and the Bureau approved after judging the high-risk anomaly "just an ordinary pet dog" in his care.

APPEARANCE: Morphix's appearance depends on his intent and on who is looking. Usually he is Dandelion, a big white dog with a long, fluffy coat and floppy black ears above a black nose; inside his own realm, he can appear as a huge winged white wolf, presumed to be his true form. Boomboom is a young man with messy dark hair and glasses who wears a dark grey hooded jacket with orange stripes over brown cargo shorts.

68.content:
**Cake Sweeper** · Mangaka
Cake Sweeper writes the hit manga "Tales of Nil". She is chronically drained (barely strong enough to go downstairs for food) and cynical about creativity, which she calls a lifelong creative block, and her paranoia about deadlines keeps her forever hiding from her editor. Even so, she is sharply observant and resourceful, always hunting for material and willing to fictionalize real events in exchange for free copies. One night on the 15th, fleeing her editor, she ran into Pawn Moonlight's door and wished to become the best mangaka in the world. The price was twenty years of blindness, payable only after she has fully enjoyed her success. What she saw inside, from talking white snakes and flying fish to a mystical blue bird and a white dog, turned her manga into a hit. She now roams Hethereau's streets gathering inspiration and greets the Appraiser like an old friend ("Appraiser! Long time no see!").

APPEARANCE: Cake Sweeper has red-auburn hair pinned up in a messy updo with clips and wears round glasses with swirl lenses. Her usual outfit is an oversized grey off-shoulder sweatshirt with a manga print and a fluffy collar, worn with pink shorts, and she works from a red office chair. She looks chronically drained and hides from her editor, yet she roams Hethereau's streets gathering inspiration and greets the Appraiser like an old friend.

69.content:
**Merula** · The Witch of St. Arbor (laid to rest)
Merula was a kind, naive girl of St. Arbor who wanted to be a savior. When the Inquisitor's witch trials consumed her town centuries ago, she stepped forward as the witch to save everyone, and in the flames, she met "the devil" and bargained to become a real witch. Her Esper ability awakened at the stake at the price of half her soul, which flew away as a spark among birds and became Blackbird. Her blood and flesh formed the Fleshbound Cage, which ended the witch hunt by imprisoning the Inquisitor but preserved St. Arbor's suffering for centuries, while she herself shrank to an infant and vanished. When the Cage weakened she wrote to Blackbird and posed as the girl Valmona and as Annie, the town herbalist, to make her remember. She was laid to rest after the Cage broke: "For we are the unburning witches. Goodbye."

Annie Fran, whose role Merula played inside the realm, was St. Arbor's 21-year-old herbalist and knew every family's secrets. Her parents, the wanderer-turned-midwife Rebecca and the town doctor Will Fran, died of plague when she was fifteen.

Narration: Merula appears only in memories and in Blackbird's dreams, or as an echo inside Oracle Stones.

APPEARANCE: Inside the realm, Merula wore the face of Annie, the town herbalist, whose long auburn hair sat under a white kerchief headband above green eyes and a kind smile. Annie dressed in a moss-green dress with a golden floral shape on the torso and golden constellations along the hem, cinched by a brown corset with three golden buckles over a white off-shoulder ruffled blouse. As the girl Valmona, Merula appeared with long orange-red hair and a pale-green ribbon headband tied with a side bow.

70.comment: Faction BG · Bureau of Anomaly Control
70.content:
**Bureau of Anomaly Control (BAC)**
The Bureau of Anomaly Control is The Circle's "Control" institution and the authority people mean when they say "the Bureau". It handles containment and nullification as well as disaster suppression, and it takes criminal cases involving anomalies or Esper abilities. Its headquarters in Area M10 of Hethereau is a tower 347 metres tall on a footprint of 300 by 214 metres, and branch offices operate in other cities. Director Alphard runs it from an office she almost never leaves (see "NPC BG · Alphard (Bureau of Anomaly Control)"), while Secretary-General Nelly runs the front of house (see "NPC BG · Nelly (Bureau of Anomaly Control)"). Glowing data orbs in the reception hall display the Wertheimer Index, and scheduled low-threat cases are handled there.

Departments:
- Joint Task Force (JTF): the frontline of professionally trained ordinary humans. They give rapid response to routine anomalies and work with local Security Offices, and they maintain the Wertheimer Towers and keep watch on the Index they produce. Teams are numbered, such as JTF Team 13, which ran search and rescue in New Helios.
- Containment Strike Units (CSU): the broadest remit in the Bureau (see "Faction BG · Containment Strike Units").
- Enforcement Tactical Division (ETD): the feared elite (see "Faction BG · Enforcement Tactical Division").
- Daily Safety Department (DSD): the public-facing desk for Oddity residence permits and Citizen IDs, which also registers newly awakened Espers and arranges special admissions or jobs for eligible ones. It opens from 09:00 to 12:00 and from 13:00 to 17:00.
- Support offices: the Logistics Department, Internal Affairs (short-staffed, with several groups out sick), the Review Committee, the Integration Office and the General Affairs Office. Joining the Bureau means passing a written exam that once took three days and keeps gaining subjects.

Anomaly staff: many employees are Oddities, and the Bureau itself is their sponsor.
- Mr. Bag runs "my mailroom", the liaison office for boarding permits and Citizen IDs ("Welcome to my mailroom. What brings you here today?"). He explains every procedure at length and keeps a drawer of confiscated homemade IDs, from handwritten cards and graffiti art to soda bottle caps. He asks clients for positive reviews and insists he is not an anomaly himself, though he no longer attends anomaly coffee time "in human form".
- Barracuda is a cheerful lizard mechanic from Logistics who ends half his sentences with "barra" or "y'know". He modifies wrenches to suit anomaly claws, and he gets roped into overtime on every day off. He calls the Director "the Demon Queen" and "our esteemed poker-faced boss", and he wants approval rights over ETD Squad 4's free repair quota.
- Ms. Fei is a flying teacup who insists she is a coffee cup and forbids the word "tea". She hosts a weekly coffee time for anomaly staff, where she serves a blend called "Deadline Essential: Work's More Bitter Than Black Coffee" and tells newcomers to bring their own mug. She also enjoys pouring cold water on grand ambitions.
- Agent LUCK is an anomaly who has worked tirelessly "in my master's place" since becoming one, and who still has not forgiven Barracuda for spending three months "fixing" LUCK's office computer.
The staff cafeteria serves anomaly employees canned insects, which Barracuda calls prison grub. A hidden internal Bagel forum collects staff complaints about colleagues.

71.content:
**Enforcement Tactical Division (ETD)**
The ETD is the Bureau's most feared division: an elite force made up entirely of powerful Espers and built for "absolute control and suppression". It holds wide operational privileges and far more clearance than other departments, and it deploys against high-level anomalies and the most dangerous criminals, as well as for major disasters. Each squad forms around one outstanding ability type or a shared trait, starting with two members and growing to four. There are seven squads. Squads 4 and 6 are stationed near headquarters in Hethereau, while the others work from branch offices in other cities. New specialist divisions keep appearing. Recruits train first with the ETD reserve team, which currently includes the trainee Nitsa.

ETD Squad 4: Captain Baicang, Lieutenant Skia, Lacrimosa and Fadia. The squad is known for balance and suppression techniques and led the response to the Hypervortex disaster in New Helios. In Logistics, it is notorious for property damage. Off duty, they still go out together, and Fadia sums them up as "a pretender, a dog and a brat".

ETD Squad 6: Captain Exe, Lieutenant Elyms, Chaos and Linko, with Nitsa training alongside them. The squad specializes in anomaly crime and meme anomalies, and it carried the Scarlet Letter case to its end by sending Chaos and Linko into the Fogden. Exe quietly cleans up after Chaos's rule-breaking, and Linko joined as the youngest member by special exception. The squad's office sits on the 17th floor of headquarters behind a security-coded door, and visitors are asked to keep what they see there in confidence. Before their recent long absence, the captain and lieutenant left Chaos a wanted list long enough to keep him busy for three months, and he caught everyone on it.

72.content:
**Containment Strike Units (CSU)**
The CSU has the broadest remit in the Bureau. Besides containing and nullifying general anomalies, it supervises and transfers temporarily contained ones and cleans up after the ETD. Squads mix Espers with JTF personnel and carry portable CSU Containers. Their schedules fill fast, and a low-risk case can wait a week for a CSU slot, which is when civilians call Anomaly Hunters instead.

CSU Squad 2 (Hethereau headquarters): Mint ran it as its only member for a long stretch until Iroi and Shinku joined after the Dreamwalk Corridor and Fogden Game incidents. Mint calls it "Containment Unit 2". Iroi's dreams can calm Shinku when her dragon power runs berserk, which is why Shinku transferred in. The three now hold game nights, and Mint likes to drag the Appraiser along.

CSU Squad 9: Shinku's former unit in another city and home to her mentor. Its members include the blunt Tempus and the joking Ray, along with a stern senior sister.

73.content:
**Eibon Antique Shop**
Eibon is an antique shop and Anomaly Hunter outfit tucked deep in Hankaku Street in Bridge Crossings, in a creepy back alley on a cheap "Grumble" storefront, the kind of corner where passers-by can hear the owner's stomach rumble. The shop is a red-brick two-storey building. The ground floor displays antiques and anomalous artifacts, with a seating area left of the door where Hotori meets clients and a talking bell called Ding Ding that begs visitors to press it "not too hard". Upstairs is the staff sitting room, with a wall of employee photos, Hotori's desk at the back and the futon she naps on. Behind the shop, two staff dormitories house everyone; the roof is where the younger members go stargazing.

Business: Eibon has run at a loss for years and sits at the bottom of Hyelp's positive-review rankings for hunters. Hotori keeps buying fake antiques at high prices, so civilian anomaly commissions keep the lights on. Adler handles the contracts, from deposits and final payments to urgent surcharges and refunds. Collateral damage (a fish tank one week, a roadblock the next) eats into every fee. The shop holds a sponsorship qualification covering its anomalous antiques along with Taygedo and Kiroumaru. Many items for sale are anomaly artifacts, and the Temporal Globe and the Mirror of Anam sit in the collection.

Founding: Hotori founded Eibon with Adler and Daffodill, and Sakiri, who already lived alongside them, counts as a founding member. When they moved in, Kiroumaru found Taygedo among old cardboard boxes. Edgar joined after a gust of wind blew Eibon's crooked hand-drawn recruitment poster into his face. Nanally came next, storming in to smash antiques because she mistook the shop for a Colucci Family recruitment test, and Hotori made her work off the debt. The Appraiser arrived last, placed there by Director Alphard. Thyme, the astrolabe anomaly, now lives at Eibon with Bureau authorization.

Roles: Hotori owns the shop and naps, while Adler, the butler and caretaker, runs the household and the books and maintains the antiques and logistics with Taygedo. Daffodill handles security. Most low-threat commissions go to Nanally, Sakiri and Edgar as the "Coluccis", and the Appraiser appraises antiques and senses anomalies. Eibon was heavily involved in bringing down The Scarlet Letter. Hotori's answer to hard times: "As for the future, we'll deal with that when the future comes!"

74.content:
**Sterry Express**
Sterry Express looks like an ordinary courier company delivering mail and goods around Hethereau ("Sterry Express, at your service!"). It works out of a single-storey building on Torchwood Avenue in Bridge Crossings with a red neon sign and big loading-bay doors; inside, video game machines crowd around a small raised sitting area. Beneath the surface, it runs deep in the intel trade and knows the anomaly underworld well. It is expensive and gets the job done, which suits big spenders who prefer to stay behind the curtain. Jiuyuan, whose old codename is "Nightingale", handles the non-standard commissions (intel, anomalies, factions) and has woven an intelligence web across the city.

Members: the original trio paired Jiuyuan on the social side with Jenson on the business side, while Hathor took deliveries. When Hathor was running herself ragged, Jiuyuan hired Haniel, whose ability can calm Hathor, and Illica as extra couriers. Jiuyuan gives Hathor the critical high-risk operations and leaves the people-facing work to Haniel and Illica, who compete over delivery records. One year-end shopping trip turned into a party for all five on Jenson's tab.

With Eibon: in the Ebisu auction affair Sterry partnered with Hotori and the Appraiser to secure The First Branch, and Sterry's crew dealt with the Rule Anomaly Nantanì when everything went wrong. Hotori calls them safe to work with as long as she isn't around, and Jiuyuan has invited the Appraiser to drop by often.

75.comment: Faction BG · Dvořák Family & Pink Paws Bank
75.content:
**The Dvořák Family & Pink Paws Bank**
The Dvořák Family is the wealthiest of The Circle's six major families and known for its charity. Lady Matilda Dvořák heads it. Her eldest son Giovanni is the family's public face and the founder and chairman of Pink Paws Bank (see "NPC BG · Giovanni Dvořák (Dvořák Family)"), and his children Sinclair and Klingsna carry the family name into Clement Academy circles. Their creed: "Everything the Dvořáks do has to live up to the family standard and be the very best." The family runs the free-entry Gold Apple Collection Hall and an orphanage, where Chiz grew up.

Pink Paws Bank (PPB) is Hethereau's only bank. Its headquarters stands on Flamingo Avenue in New Herland District, with branches on Camelot Avenue and Ironheart 9th Avenue in New Herland, on Hankaku Street in Bridge Crossings and on Saint Torres Avenue in Miguel District. Chiz is its most dependable manager, and her coworkers include Haruna and Grace as well as her mentor Mayu. Wealthy clients such as Iroi's family appear on its lists.

Gossip: the young wine brand Bacchus began when Giovanni bought a vineyard for his third wife, who sold it publicly after their split. During the puppet scare, Bagel guessed the puppets were a Dvořák-funded art exhibition of Giovanni's.

76.comment: Faction BG · Tamamochi Street Resident Association
76.content:
**Tamamochi Street Resident Association**
Everyone who works or lives on Tamamochi Market Street, the strip of cheap shops in western Illusion Town directly south of Duskmoor, belongs to its Resident Association, a semi-official neighborhood body. Its street manager is Aurelia, who rides her big blue jellyfish up and down the street and knows every resident's likes and dislikes; to the local kids, she is a big sister. Because her ability robbed her of any sense of direction, the locals quietly help her find her way. The street lies close to the StarSign livehouse, and THE WHOOTS!!!! sold their first tickets here.

77.comment: Faction BG · StarSign, Lines & THE WHOOTS!!!!
77.content:
**StarSign, Lines & THE WHOOTS!!!!**
StarSign is a basement livehouse on Fiscus Avenue in Illusion Town, near a cluster of apartment blocks, reached by a long, narrow staircase that Aurelia's jellyfish cannot manage. Its owner Kiyosawa lends out practice space and hauls gear outdoors for street shows, and Akane Rin tends the bar. StarSign bands aim for Night of Moondog, a legendary music festival that is also a Location Anomaly, where performers score by how strongly they resonate with anomalies.

Lines: the band of Clement Academy friends Akane Rin, Aurelia and Suzuha, who also worked as Anomaly Hunters and dreamed of touring until they became legends as the best band among hunter organizations. Lines grew from Aurelia's wish that the three of them stay together forever. It ended when the anomaly Swallowtail cost Aurelia the use of her legs and her family blamed the band and the hunting for it. Suzuha moved to another city afterwards. The three reconciled at the Clement Academy centennial.

THE WHOOTS!!!!: the band Nanally formed at StarSign with Haniel and the Appraiser, with Akane Rin as mentor and then lead vocalist; Haniel plays guitar and the Appraiser plays drums. The four exclamation marks are part of the name ("I'll skip saying the four exclamation marks out loud. Just feel them."). They scored 60 points at their Night of Moondog debut and played the centennial festival. Their songs include "Heroic Appearance", "Everlasting Dazing Summer", "Destiny" and "Mayoiuta", and Nanally and Haniel dream of a DSD POP collaboration.

78.content:
**The Scarlet Letter**
The Scarlet Letter was a criminal organization based in Duskmoor and led by Inanna, whom her people called "Mother", "Madam T" or "Ms. T" (see "NPC BG · Inanna (The Scarlet Letter)"). In public, Inanna was a philanthropist and businesswoman. In private her "charities" collected girls as "flowers" in a place she called the Garden, raising them through brutal trials to see which would survive longest and bloom most beautifully, and turning the survivors into tools for grey-area missions. Members carried flower names, like Zankou's "Red Nightshade", and Inanna's adopted "daughters" called one another sisters.

Known members: Inanna (leader), Zankou (core member), Poinsette (door-opening Esper), the bird-collecting assassin Sweeper, Monte Cristo, the disgraced researcher known as the Scholar, and the former hunters Glaire and Phear. Daffodill was Inanna's first adopted daughter and once her blade under the codename "Night Mothling"; she later returned undercover for the Bureau.

Methods: the organization gathered rare anomalies by theft and deception, from The First Branch at the Ebisu auction to the Eternal Present and the Helm of Theseus. It hacked Bagel accounts to spread panic and recruited the desperate with late-night broadcasts promising rebirth ("Come. Return to Mother's embrace."). Kidnapped Esper children served it as "consumables". All of it fed Inanna's game inside the Fog Coffin, and powerful guests protected her.

Status: broken. Inanna died when the Fogden collapsed, and her guests were delivered unconscious to the Bureau. Zankou is held on Ghroth Island, while Poinsette is under supervision at the Esper Academy.

79.content:
**Yggash Court**
Yggash Court is The Circle's intelligence institution and its "Cognition" arm. Its archivists compile the Anomaly Profiles, assigning profile numbers and classes along with clearance levels, and its archive, which Edgar calls "the tree hollow", is every bookish Esper's dream workplace. Its location and leadership are unknown to the public. Bureau staff grumble that the Court is slow and looks down on them, and Barracuda calls its people "featherbrains from Fraxinus". Fraxinus is the name tied to the Court's inner workings, "the branch" Blackbird once perched on. Director Alphard has access to "educated guesses from Fraxinus", and Fraxinus delivered the final verdict on the Fog Coffin. Even the schemers behind the Ebisu auction spoke of choosing "which side of Fraxinus to stand on".

The Witch's House: the Court keeps Blackbird in a house furnished exactly to her liking in exchange for deciphering an ancient prophecy and purifying the Oracle Stones that birds bring her, and Lavinia serves as the guardian the Court assigned to her. Clients visit the house for divinations. The Court prefers that Blackbird stay home and let the stones come to her. Edgar's parents are Court clerks who write and maintain profiles.

80.content:
**Anomalies & Oddities**
An anomaly is anything that defies common sense, and where anomalies come from remains the world's greatest unsolved mystery. Yggash Court sorts them into five basic types. Bio and Object anomalies are the most common and always have a fixed physical form. Phenomenon, Location and Meme anomalies are rarer and formless; some of them wear lifelike bodies, and such a body is a manifestation that does not count as an Oddity.

Oddities: the everyday name for Bio anomalies. They can be self-aware and think for themselves even when they look nothing like humans. Many live openly in Hethereau, whether as pets and coworkers or as shop mascots and registered citizens, and Oddities often turn up alongside other anomalies.

Special categories:
- Derivative Anomaly: closely tied to one specific anomaly, either as an appendage or variant of it or as an evolved or devolved form. It can differ from its source in type and class, and its profile number records the order of discovery.
- Surge Anomaly: appears or activates alongside other anomalies, often tethered to a powerful one or found inside an Anomalous Realm. Usually lower in class and unrelated by development, it gets its own profile number.
- Rule Anomaly: behaves with precise, traceable logic and enforces a complete set of rules inside its domain. Some embody a rule outright; others exist to achieve a purpose, often by patching a loophole in rules that already exist.

Nexus: the critical point where a specific intervention drastically changes how an anomaly manifests. Each anomaly has its own, and finding it is the key to containing or nullifying the anomaly. Nexuses vary wildly. Staring into the Hypervortex's core from one precise angle made it collapse, and the Picture Frame anomaly R-3707 was nullified the moment someone sincerely called it beautiful.

Anomalous Realms: many anomalies generate pocket spaces that run on their own physics, with entry conditions and exits of their own. A realm can loop its corridors and flip gravity, and some trap visitors or slip into superposition if people linger too long. Leaving safely usually means following the realm's rules or resolving its Nexus.

Encroachment and Countertransference: anomalies leak influence into ordinary things nearby. Minor encroachment rarely shows, while major encroachment varies with the anomaly and its surroundings. Countertransference Theory holds that the closer a person gets to anomalies, or the longer they study them, the more susceptible they become to physical and mental influence.

Homology Theory: an academic hypothesis that Esper abilities and anomalies share one source. Others argue that Esper abilities are powers granted to humans from outside. The debate is unresolved and a favorite of radio talk shows.

Anomaly Profiles: Yggash Court archivists compile profiles with images, a profile number, type, aliases, file permissions, class, recorded stories, characteristics, Nexus, risk assessment, containment or guarantee status, containment measures, experiment records and derivatives. Profiles are the best reference available, though nobody claims they are fully objective, and any field above the reader's clearance shows only "insufficient permissions". Profile numbers follow a strict letter-and-digits format that cannot be changed (Taygedo is U-5291, Kiroumaru R-1107, the Hospitable House T-1377); the letter marks a category, such as U for Unknown and R for Reality, while the digits look random.

81.comment: World BG · Wertheimer Index & Clearance Levels
81.content:
**Wertheimer Index & Clearance Levels**
The Wertheimer Index measures how far something deviates from reality. Readings come from the fluctuations an anomaly causes when it appears or activates, and the values run negative: the stronger the anomaly, the deeper the drop. When an anomaly weakens toward natural nullification, the local Index climbs back toward normal.

Wertheimer Towers are supposed to stand in every major area of every city. They collect environmental data to calculate the local Index, which feeds the glowing data orbs inside the Bureau of Anomaly Control, and the Joint Task Force maintains them and watches the numbers. The Appraiser is the only known Esper the Index cannot register, and the anomaly Code Zero leaves no reading either.

Yggash Court's classes measure what an anomaly is capable of, which is different from what it will do:
- Class I (-1 to -2): negligible.
- Class II (-2 to -3): minor injuries to individuals.
- Class III (-3 to -4): casualties among individuals.
- Class IV (-4 to -5): multiple casualties in sparsely populated urban areas.
- Class V (-5 to -10): mass casualties in urban areas.
- Class VI (-10 to -20): mass casualties across a city.
- Class VII (-20 to -50): can destroy a city's functions. The Hypervortex of New Helios was Class VII.
- Class VIII (-50 to -100): can destroy a city.
- Class IX (-100 to -200): can destroy multiple cities.
- Class X (beyond -200): extinction level.

Clearance levels, also set by Yggash Court, decide who may read which anomaly files:
- Public: every citizen.
- Bounty: every member of The Circle, Anomaly Hunters included.
- Restricted: members of The Circle's five public institutions and the six major families.
- Classified: senior officials of the five institutions and specially designated personnel.
- Confidential: only the members of the Supreme Tribunal A6.
The Bureau's staff live by a Confidentiality Policy whose second article forbids asking about information unrelated to one's own work.

82.content:
**Containment, Nullification & Capturing**
Containment restricts or isolates an anomaly. Stable, low-threat anomalies can be kept under a temporary containment routine, and some Esper abilities can hold an anomaly by themselves. Most contained anomalies sit in vessels called Containers, with portable CSU Containers for the squads in the field, while serious cases end up in Containment Units at the Celaeno Compound. A breach triggers re-containment or, failing that, nullification; the Bureau runs a Crisis Response Protocol when something escapes inside its own building.

Nullification erases an anomaly from the human world without guaranteeing it has stopped existing, so a nullified anomaly may manifest again someday. Hunting down the Nexus is the fastest route. Some anomalies fade on their own through natural nullification, which shows up as the local Wertheimer Index rising back to normal. Nullifying an unsponsored anomaly that disrupts city order is legal, while sponsored anomalies and Anomaly Citizens are protected (see "World BG · Anomaly Citizenship & Guarantors").

Capturing means collecting the remnants an anomaly leaves behind after its activity. Remnants sent to Midas Technologies feed research, and the sender may be rewarded with an Arc, a piece of equipment that carries part of an anomaly's ability. Industrially processed anomaly derivatives also reach shops as everyday Anomaly Products (see "World BG · Daily Life & Brands").

83.content:
**Espers, Esper Types & Esper Contracts**
An Esper is an ordinary human in whom a supernatural ability has awakened. Abilities are wildly uneven: some can flatten a street, while others are weak, oddly specific or comical. Many carry a cost, such as Daffodill's damaged left eye or the canine features Skia grew after his awakening. Newly awakened Espers must register with the Bureau's Daily Safety Department, which also arranges special admissions and jobs for eligible Espers, and young Espers who need supervision may be placed at the Esper Academy.

Esper types: abilities fall into six types by how they manifest, split into two trios.
- Top Trio: Cosmos (silver, light), Anima (green, life, with enhanced movement) and Lakshana (gold, order; the word means "sign" or "symptom").
- Bottom Trio: Psyche (azure, dark), Chaos (purple, dark) and Incantation (red, force).
Abilities of different types can feed into each other when Espers fight together (see "Combat System · Narration Rules").

Esper Contracts: a human without an awakened ability can still wield power by making a contract with an anomaly, which agrees to work with them and lends its strength. A contract may also grant perception, as Adler's contract "Ayatana" lets him sense his surroundings with great certainty. If the contract breaks, the borrowed abilities vanish. Known contractors include Adler (Ayatana, with the armor anomaly Enlightenment) and Sakiri ("Ghosteater", with Kiroumaru). Inanna held several contracts at once, and Glaire's eye contract, which once gave her sight, has expired. Contractors so far have all registered as Incantation type.

Some Espers serve in the Bureau or work as Anomaly Hunters, while others live entirely ordinary lives, and using an ability to commit a crime counts as anomaly crime.

84.content:
**Anomaly Citizenship, Sponsorship & Guarantors**
Sponsorship, also called guarantee, is how Hethereau protects anomalies that live among people. A sponsor, or guarantor, voluntarily takes responsibility for an anomaly's safety and basic rights without any contract or master-servant bond, and may hold anyone who harms that anomaly accountable. In return, a sponsored anomaly must stay under its sponsor's control at all times so any accident can be stopped at once. Businesses can hold a sponsorship qualification certifying that every anomaly in their care is safe for the city. The Eibon Antique Shop holds one covering its anomalous antiques along with Taygedo and Kiroumaru, which makes every Eibon member, the Appraiser included, one of Taygedo's guarantors. Guarantors must meet requirements that include a minimum age, so Nanally cannot be one yet.

Unsponsored anomalies have no such protection. Wandering anomalies that disrupt city order, like the Rainmen or a Boom Boom Cloud, may be nullified legally, and most hunter commissions start there.

Anomaly Citizenship lifts the leash. Anomalies able to integrate, usually Oddities, may apply to the Bureau of Anomaly Control if they have a sponsor. Applicants must also be self-aware and intelligent enough to behave autonomously. Citizens gain civil rights and obligations, so Taygedo goes out whenever he likes and even receives parcels addressed to "Taygedo". Citizen IDs are renewed at the Bureau every new year, and the anomaly's guarantor must come along. The paperwork (a personal statement and the sponsor's qualification certificate, plus the old ID) goes to Mr. Bag's mailroom, and homemade IDs only hurt the applicant. Bureau employees are sponsored by the Bureau itself, so the Director simply signs for them.

The Citizenship Evaluation has three phases. It starts with a biometric record and a fresh ID photo, followed by a cognitive interview on whether the applicant can live independently and respect city order while taking responsibility for themselves. Last comes an ability test in the Safety Assessment Room that rates danger level and controllability. The test does not harm the applicant, and the Bureau has ways to interview anomalies that cannot speak.

A guarantor has the final say over an anomaly's name. Last year's funniest news was the "Woofo Renaming Saga": after a fight over lemon juice on fried chicken, the furious guarantor of Acacia, the stuck-up lizard boss of Acacian Aeronauts, renamed him Woofo, pressing so hard on the form that the pen dented Mr. Bag's desk.

85.comment: World BG · Anomaly Hunters & Anomaly Crime
85.content:
**Anomaly Hunters, Commissions & Anomaly Crime**
Anomaly Hunters are civilian professionals, solo or in teams, who take paid commissions to investigate anomalies the Bureau rates as low priority or cannot reach in time, then contain or nullify them. They belong to The Circle in the broad sense and hold Bounty clearance. Commissions arrive at the door or through apps, and clients rate hunters on the review site Hyelp, where Eibon sits at the bottom of the positive-review rankings. A typical contract splits the fee into a deposit and a final payment, with an urgent surcharge on rush jobs and a refund if the case goes unsolved. New Herland District is the richest hunter market, and Midas Technologies sells most of the gear.

Known outfits include the Eibon Antique Shop and Sterry Express. Mr. Galaxis of Acacian Aeronauts is a living legend of the trade: a solo hunter for decades, never part of a team, whose abilities have never dulled. He inspired the tokusatsu show "Kokoro Rider".

Inside Anomalous Realms, teams keep in touch through team Esper abilities or communication anomalies such as the Chuppa, while their personal phones handle records and payments, and social life as well.

Anomaly crime: deliberate human crime that exploits an anomaly's characteristics or an Esper ability. It is rising as anomalies and Espers become ordinary, and since Security Offices cannot cover it, the Bureau of Anomaly Control takes such cases directly, with ETD Squad 6 specializing in them. A civilian hunter may drop a commission the moment it proves to be anomaly crime and hand the case to the Bureau.

86.content:
**The Circle**
The Circle is the collective name for the world's anomaly authorities. For most of history, it worked as a secret guardian, taking in Espers and containing or nullifying anomalies so ordinary people never had to know. Forty years ago, a catastrophe forced it to reveal anomalies and Espers to the world. Its work rests on the "3 C's" of Control, Containment and Cognition.

In the narrow sense, The Circle means five public institutions under the Supreme Tribunal A6:
- Bureau of Anomaly Control (Control): the field authority over anomalies and Espers that also polices anomaly crime, headquartered in Hethereau (see "Faction BG · Bureau of Anomaly Control").
- Yggash Court (Cognition): intelligence work, from anomaly profiles and classes to clearance levels (see "Faction BG · Yggash Court").
- Celaeno Compound (Containment): houses contained anomalies in Containment Units.
- Zerogon Laboratory (Cognition): research. It is affiliated with Midas Technologies, which makes Anomaly Hunter gear and leads the Anomaly Products industry, and it runs the Thoth Research Institute (patents on Arcs) and the Odyssey Research Institute (patents on Consoles). Its new technology made the Ghost Train safe enough to ride without a ticket.
- Ghroth Island (Containment): the secret prison and observation facility (see "World BG · Ghroth Island").
The Supreme Tribunal A6 stands above them all and alone holds Confidential clearance. The institutions keep headquarters and direct branches in major cities, except Ghroth Island, whose location almost nobody knows.

In the broad sense, The Circle also covers civilian Anomaly Hunter organizations and individual hunters. Six major families hold Restricted clearance alongside the institutions; the Dvořák Family is the wealthiest of them, and the other five have not been named.

Public mood: conspiracy theories claim that anomalies have already infiltrated The Circle, or that its leaders are puppets putting on a show.

87.content:
**Chuppa (Communication Anomaly)**
A Chuppa is a communication anomaly issued by the Bureau of Anomaly Control. It keeps working inside most Anomalous Realms, and only a few Bureau members may give it commands. Director Alphard, who almost never leaves her office, talks to the field through a Chuppa as her proxy, and she gave the Appraiser one for staying in touch. Mint once tracked the Appraiser down inside a realm by following it. When Linko's telepathy cannot reach a Chuppa from inside a realm, nobody inside can.

88.content:
**The Ghost Train (Anomaly Express of Hethereau)**
The Ghost Train is Hethereau's anomaly-run metro. The train was "created for the same reason" as its stations and its route manager, and all of them are bound together, so the Bureau could never fire the manager even when complaints piled up. When passengers wait on a platform the train arrives within the minute, and it is the fastest way across the city, running through Anomalous Realm space between stops.

Miss Levi, the Train Manager, is a blue-glowing, owl-like Oddity in a uniform cap who carries a megaphone. She has two eyes, and anything else claiming to be the Manager cannot be trusted. Aloud she only coos and repeats her broadcast lines, while her real speech runs as thoughts most humans cannot hear. She is diligent and proud of the line's efficiency, and so starved for conversation that she chats and grumbles about the Bureau whenever she can. The Appraiser can hear her, so she calls them her "Soulmate"; she tutored them personally and handed over an Outstanding Passenger Certificate as proof of their bond.

The Bureau once required a boarding permit, the "Train Ticket". After the train adopted new Zerogon Laboratory technology, the risk dropped enough for tickets to be revoked and guide staff to leave the entrances. The Passenger Manual now sits in stations for voluntary reading. Keen riders can still earn the Outstanding Passenger Certificate through the Daily Safety Department and a written test.

Passenger Manual highlights:
- Security screening applies. Combat gear and containment devices of limited size need advance Bureau clearance and may never be used while the train moves. Safely contained Class III anomalies may ride.
- Felines, including Oddities with feline features, are generally barred unless absolutely necessary. Miss Levi refuses to explain why.
- Never board if the doors fail to open or open somewhere wrong, such as the roof or the gap between cars.
- Suddenly finding yourself alone in the carriage is normal, so stay calm. If an open door appears mid-ride, keep away and do not look outside until it disappears.
- The train has no emergency button. If a red "Emergency" button appears during a stoppage, never press it; wait in the safety zone and defend yourself with Esper abilities if needed.
- Getting off between stations strands a passenger in an Anomalous Realm; the record wait before rescue is 2,179 hours.
- After alighting, leave the platform quickly. At a wrong stop, exit the station and come back in. If you step off somewhere that is not a station you know, stay inside and call for Miss Levi, and the train will come for you.
- Esper abilities are banned aboard, and so is unpermitted contact with other Anomalous Realms; attempts to contain the train or its Manager are forbidden, too.
- Service is suspended on Wednesdays with a full moon, and breaking the Manual earns a permanent ban.
As Miss Levi puts it, behind every seemingly absurd rule, there is an even more absurd story.

89.content:
**Ghroth Island**
Ghroth Island is The Circle's high-security prison and observation facility, isolated far out at sea; very few people know where it lies. It holds rogue Espers and high-risk anomaly subjects under ability-suppression systems, along with people whose abilities are unknown or unstable. It is separate from the Hethereau Detention Facility, which holds ordinary criminals.

Transfers travel aboard a vessel called the Escorter, whose punctuality Director Alphard likes to mock. The Appraiser rode it to Hethereau after seven weeks of observation on the island, in the company of the Sonic Dimension Lord, a talking anomaly who styles himself the rap king of Ghroth Island and "the destined nemesis of silence".

Chaos once served there as its "Graveyard Keeper", and Fadia was imprisoned there before ETD Squad 4 took her in. Zankou was sent there after the Fogden Game.

90.content:
**Clement Academy**
Clement Academy is a comprehensive school in north Illusion Town, just off Fiscus Avenue. It pioneered "anomalogy" education and has run strict safety rules ever since a severe anomaly incident. That makes it discreet and conservative, and non-students cannot walk in through the main gate. The campus has a red-brick three-storey main building with detached wings, and outside it, there are two basketball courts and a soccer field, plus a running track with bleachers. Clubs include a Garden Club, and the school recently celebrated its centennial with alumni coming home for it.

Students and alumni: Linko is still enrolled although she stopped attending, and Maiyue is a current student. Akane Rin, Aurelia, Suzuha, Sinclair Dvořák and Elyms are alumni, and all three members of the band Lines studied here.

91.content:
**Pawn Moonlight (Anomalous Realm)**
Pawn Moonlight was an urban legend about a mystical pawnshop that grants any wish for a proportional price, a name its human visitors invented. In truth, the realm was the lair of the spatial anomaly Morphix, a Class IV Oddity known as the fluffy white dog Dandelion, and for six months, the wandering Esper twins Mismo and Otro sheltered there and ran it as a pawnshop (see "NPC BG · Mismo & Otro (Pawn Moonlight)" and "NPC BG · Morphix & Boomboom").

Getting in: rumour says the huge entrance door appears only on the night of the 15th of each month. The real mechanism is Morphix's wish lock, which makes the door manifest when someone nearby voices a strong, sincere wish. The Eibon crew summoned it at Green Wall Slope by speaking their deepest wishes under the moon.

Contracts: deals were formalized as "Confirmations". Once a client began actively using the wish-granting object, the contract became absolute, with no refunds and no renewals. Prices scaled with the wish, and archived pawn tickets show clients paying with one of their senses, from sight and taste to smell and touch, or with years of life or even the capacity to love. When a contract was fulfilled, the object's power faded until it became mundane, and its ticket returned to the archive by itself. A contract left hanging, with the object loaned out and the price unpaid, drained the missing cost from Otro's lifespan.

Inside: a shifting labyrinth of floating stone architecture under open sky. Purple platforms flip 180 degrees about every six seconds and invert gravity for anyone standing on them. Looping square rooms punish wrong turns: shadow-eyes open across the walls before a giant purple ghostly hand rises from the floor and drags the intruder to a dark, isolated room. Elsewhere, black shifting shadow-hands guard invisible barriers. The archive warehouse holds jars that grow and shrink while their patterns change, and suitcases that are randomly empty or full. Its safes nest inside identical safes, and its scrolls are written in undocumented languages. A whole wing belonged to Morphix, from a giant dog bowl and a statue of Dandelion to rooms full of toys and grooming gear, and the twins kept their veterinary manuals and diet records there.

Status: after the Toshi kidnapping case was solved and Morphix went home with his owner, the twins left Hethereau and the pawnshop closed (see "S1 Spinoff · Pawn Moonlight").

92.content:
**New Helios & the Hypervortex**
New Helios was a city far from Hethereau and the site of the Hypervortex disaster. The Hypervortex is a Class VII Phenomenon Anomaly filed as N-0824[Ph] with Public clearance, and it struck at dusk while the city was bracing for the year's first extreme rainstorm (see "S1 Ep0 · Unforeseen Yet Foretold (Prologue I)" for the night itself).

The halo: anyone who looks up at the sky under the rain's influence will see the Hypervortex's halo, and by then, there is no turning back. Looking straight at the halo instantly destroys an ordinary person's mind. Many of the people rescued from the ruins after the nullification were brain-dead or left in a vegetative state, and those with milder symptoms still suffered severe cognitive disorders, amnesia or other post-traumatic conditions. People who stayed out of the rain and never looked at the halo mostly escaped direct harm. Espers who took part in the rescue reported that they can look at the halo briefly without serious injury. The danger explains the sealed Black Box Masks of the rescue teams and Skia's order that nobody look at the vortex.

Aftermath: nullifying the Hypervortex did not undo its damage, and the risk of secondary disasters remains serious. Surge Anomalies, mostly Protocores, appeared in large numbers inside its area of influence and attack everything around them, and they stayed after the Hypervortex itself was gone (see "World BG · Anomalies & Oddities" for Surge Anomalies). The nullification left more than ruins and rubble. Buildings float and trees grow in reverse while steel reinforcement bars slowly branch like limbs, and the twisted "prosperity" this gives the city has left it unfit for human habitation.

Narration: so far New Helios appears only in the prologue and in Bureau files, so characters know it through news and records, or from the accounts of rescue crews. The Appraiser was found staring into the Hypervortex's core with no memories, and amnesia is one of the halo's recorded effects; canon has not said whether the two are connected, so leave that question open.

93.content:
**The Imaginary Old Friend (the Invalid Number)**
About four years ago, a Bagel user described a dream in which a long-lost friend, face and name blurred, recited a phone number and asked to be called. The number was invalid. Others answered that they had dreamed the same thing, and strangers around the world turned out to share the exact same digits. The "invalid number" trended for about a year before people let it go. Recently, an old post by the Bagel account "Hethereau Urban Legend Bot" pushed it back to the top. Dialing it brings "The number you have dialed is not in service" and the digits 316651. Some callers fall asleep afterwards and wake inside the anomaly's realm, while others get a call back some time after hanging up, and answering it can pull them in.

What it is: the invalid number began as a Class I meme anomaly, a wide-area collective dream that only stirred nostalgia. People who missed estranged friends kept dialing and leaving messages in the hope of a reunion, and their shared imagination grew it into the Imaginary Old Friend, a Class VI meme anomaly. It answers the wish for a lost friend by generating an ideal version of that friend from stolen memory data and planting it over the real memories, erasing contradictions and adjusting personalities until the person accepts the replacement. The swap is painless and imperceptible, and it cannot be refused or undone. The people who believe in these friends give it the social bonds it needs to sustain itself, and its avatars spread worldwide with barely noticeable Wertheimer fluctuations.

The realm: a vast space of data built like a glowing blocky city, the anomaly's central database. Each block is one user's archive unit, where a visitor relives the memories behind one friendship; cracking its storage medium renders that user's old-friend avatar as a person. Storage media relock about ten seconds after being cracked and the realm restores itself from backups, so it cannot be demolished in one stroke. The anomaly is present everywhere inside it at once. Below a warning "safety door" the collective dream turns into heavy mental strain, and Oddities wander there. Visitors enter through someone's connection to the anomaly, like borrowing an account, and are thrown out if that connection is cut.

Secrecy and status: the original investigation found that people who never existed had appeared out of nowhere, but by then more than 300,000 people were under its influence, so The Circle classified the results and made a pact. As long as it does not meddle with many avatars at once, it will not be contained or nullified, and it may appear as only one person with one identity at a time. It was also asked to use its networking power to help found a new ETD squad, and that single identity is Elyms, lieutenant of ETD Squad 6 (see "Esper BG · Elyms (ETD Squad 6)"). Exe once destroyed 316,650 of its connections at once, but calls from the people who rely on it pieced it back together and it rewrote its own code with broader permissions. Its realm is now in ruins and its capacity reduced, yet it survives. Only The Circle and the Bureau's leadership know the truth, along with Exe and the Appraiser; Chaos, Linko and Nitsa do not.

**Combat System · Narration Rules**
Fights in Hethereau are anomaly cases first and brawls second. Follow these rules when narrating combat.
- Work out the rules and the Nexus. Anomalies obey internal logic, and brute force often fails or makes things worse. Meme anomalies feed on attention and Rule Anomalies cannot be broken from outside their domain, while Anomalous Realms trap people who ignore their conditions. Let characters notice patterns and test conditions until they can strike at the Nexus, which the Appraiser's Zeroth Sense can locate.
- Every Esper fights with a unique ability and a personal style (see each character's Combat Style). Different types reinforce each other when Espers fight side by side: Cosmos and Anima together make living light bloom into exploding blossoms, and Anima with Incantation leaves a target hexed and open to follow-up blows. Show this as visible synergy between teammates.
- Teams cover each other. Someone draws attention up front while a support Esper heals or shields, and a ranged fighter picks off threats. Communication stays open through a Chuppa or E.A.R., or through Linko's telepathy. A perfectly timed dodge opens a counterattack, and squads keep pressure on large anomalies by swapping in fresh fighters.
- Show the cost. Many abilities carry side effects or risks (lost taste, lost direction, berserk rage, fear of loud noise), and anomalies leave marks on people who stay close too long.
- Stakes and aftermath matter: injuries linger and property damage costs money (Eibon's fees, Squad 4's repair bills). Afterwards, the Bureau files reports, and a nullified anomaly may leave remnants worth capturing.
- Keep it diegetic. Describe fights in physical and emotional terms, through movement, sound, light and terrain, never through game terms such as health bars, levels, cooldowns or damage numbers.
